desc: D4 CONFIRMED: iOS UIBackgroundModes is entirely absent — the app cannot run in the background on iOS, making the wake-up alarm non-functional on the platform.
ev: ios/Runner/Info.plist lines 4-60 contain no UIBackgroundModes key (grep for UIBackgroundModes/BGTaskScheduler/audio across Info.plist + *.swift returned nothing). AppDelegate.swift (all 13 lines) has no CLLocationManager/allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates/BGTaskScheduler. No .entitlements file exists under ios/.
fix: Add UIBackgroundModes array with `location` (and `audio` if the alarm must sound through screen-off) to Info.plist; in native code set CLLocationManager.allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates=true and pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically=false, or adopt significant-location-change / region monitoring. This is a substantial native iOS build, not a config tweak — realistically iOS should be descoped from v1 for a solo/budget founder.

desc: No battery-optimization / Doze exemption is ever requested (REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS missing) — on Xiaomi/MIUI and Samsung/OneUI the foreground service is killed during a long screen-off journey, so the live-notification alarm fires late or never.
ev: grep for REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS/isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations/requestDisable across android/ and lib/ returned nothing. AndroidManifest.xml has no such permission. permission_service.dart requests only location/notification/activity. battery_plus is level-read only (homescreen.dart L65).
fix: Add REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS to the manifest and prompt via an ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS intent (or a plugin) during onboarding; add OEM-specific autostart/'no restrictions' deep-link guidance for MIUI/OneUI. Essential for India-first Android reliability.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: No uncertainty-aware / critical-fractile firing. The alarm fires on the point (median) ETA or exact geometric stop count with no k*sigma pessimistic lead, even though both sigmaEta and EKF.sigmaS are computed and available.
ev: EtaEngine returns sigmaEta (eta_engine.dart:536-548,561) but no code reads it (grep for sigmaEta/result.sigma consumers outside eta_engine.dart is empty; location_stream_handler.dart:362-363 keeps only etaSeconds+vEst). EKF.sigmaS only logged (trackingservice.dart:2221) / snapshotted (location_stream_handler.dart:403). Time-mode fires on `smoothedETA <= threshold` (alarm_controller.dart:680-682); metro stops fire on `remainingStopsToTarget <= N` (alarm_evaluator.dart:796-797).
fix: Fire on a pessimistic quantile: trigger when (etaSeconds + z*sigmaEta) <= leadSeconds (z from EKF/GPS confidence). For stops, inflate the effective position by z*EKF.sigmaS before counting stops, so a station-scale position error fires one stop early rather than late. Plumb result.sigmaEta and EkfPublicState.sigmaS into AlarmContext.

desc: Wrong-direction (rider boards opposite-direction train / walks the wrong way) is never detected or surfaced, and on metro legs is silently clamped so the destination alarm stalls forever instead of warning.
ev: grep for wrong.direction/reverse/opposite across lib/ finds NO wrong-direction feature. Off-route detection is lateral-offset-only: deviation_detection.dart:60-66 and deviation_monitor.dart:52-123 key entirely off offsetMeters (distance from the polyline), never direction of travel. A reverse rider on the same metro corridor has a tiny lateral offset, so no deviation/reroute fires. Progress cannot correct it either: snap_to_route.dart:172 adds +100 score as 'Hard resistance to backward movement' and :202-204 adds +50 reverse-lane penalty; and ekf_pipeline.dart:204-208 hard-clamps metro legs — `if(!_allowReverse){ if(_v<0)_v=0; if(_s<sOld)_s=sOld; }` — with allowReverse set false for every metro leg (ekf_orchestrator.dart:288 `_pipeline.setAllowReverse(!isMetroLeg)`). Net: a sleeping rider who boards the wrong-direction train at an interchange has progress frozen at the boarding point, the 'N stops / distance / time before destination' alarm never reaches threshold, and no wrong-way alert is ever raised.
fix: Add a signed along-track velocity / heading-vs-route-bearing check that is independent of lateral offset. When sustained progress is negative or heading opposes segment bearing (snap_to_route already computes segment bearing at :202) beyond a debounce, raise an explicit 'you may be going the wrong way' notification rather than clamping. Do NOT hard-freeze `s` on metro legs without also emitting a reverse-detected signal to the alarm/UI layer.

desc: No battery-optimization / Doze exemption is ever requested (D1 confirmed). No REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission and no runtime prompt anywhere; PermissionService stops at location+notification+activity (permission_service.dart:13-99).
ev: grep for IGNORE_BATTERY/BATTERY_OPTIMIZ across android/ and lib/ returns zero hits. AndroidManifest.xml lines 3-13 list all permissions; battery optimization is not among them. permission_service.dart requestEssentialPermissions() (lines 13-26) requests only location, notification, activity-recognition. On Xiaomi/MIUI, Samsung, Oppo/Vivo/OnePlus the app is left in the OS-managed 'optimized' bucket, so a screen-off foreground service on a 2h idle journey is a prime candidate for Doze/OEM kill.
fix: Add REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS to the manifest and, right after granting location, call Permission.ignoreBatteryOptimizations.request() (permission_handler already in pubspec). Add an onboarding step that deep-links into OEM autostart/battery screens (e.g. via a MIUI/Samsung intent map or a package like disable_battery_optimization). Detect optimization state on each startTracking and warn the user before they sleep.

desc: Alarm sound and the alarm notification are delegated from the background isolate to the (possibly dead) UI isolate. When the rider swipes the app away, the background service survives but the alarm becomes silent and invisible.
ev: alarm_controller.dart:277-286 triggerAlarmNotification: `if (isBackgroundIsolate) { service.invoke('triggerAlarm', ...) }` with the comment 'Always delegate sound playback to the foreground isolate.' It does NOT call showWakeUpAlarm in the background branch, so neither the notification nor the sound is produced by the background isolate. The invoke is received only by ForegroundBridge._handleTriggerAlarm (foreground_bridge.dart:203-233), whose onAlarmTrigger listener lives in the UI isolate. The actual sound is AlarmPlayer.playSelected() run in-process (notification_service.dart:795-796) with the notification itself set playSound:false (line 728). Swiping from recents destroys the Activity/UI engine, so the delegated invoke has no live listener -> no sound, no full-screen intent. This is the exact sleeping-rider-swiped-away case.
fix: In the background branch of triggerAlarmNotification, show the full-screen high-importance alarm notification directly (with a channel-backed alarm sound via RawResourceAndroidNotificationSound, not only the in-process AlarmPlayer) instead of relying on service.invoke to the UI. Keep the foreground path as an enhancement, not the sole delivery mechanism.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: No self-contained background alarm: the entire alarm raise (sound + notification + full-screen intent) is delegated from the background isolate to the UI isolate via a fire-and-forget service.invoke('triggerAlarm') with no ACK, retry, or fallback. If the UI isolate is dead — the dominant case for a 2h screen-off journey on Xiaomi/Samsung, which aggressively kill the cached app process while the foreground service persists — the invoke is dropped and NOTHING sounds, shows, or wakes the screen.
ev: alarm_controller.dart:277-286 (if isBackgroundIsolate → only service.invoke('triggerAlarm'), no direct show/play); foreground_bridge.dart:73,203-233 (receiver lives in UI isolate); trackingservice.dart:150-166 (onAlarmTrigger→showWakeUpAlarm wired in UI isolate). Unlike invokeWithAckRetry used for route registration (foreground_bridge.dart:265-311), the triggerAlarm invoke has no ACK/retry. The bg-side re-post safety net ensureAlarmNotificationVisible is gated on pending_alarm_flag (notification_service.dart:854), which is only ever set inside showWakeUpAlarm (notification_service.dart:713) — i.e. only after the FOREGROUND already ran — so it cannot resurrect an alarm the dead foreground never showed.
fix: When isBackgroundIsolate, post the notification AND start audio/vibration directly from the background isolate (flutter_local_notifications and the native haptics channel both work in the bg isolate; test whether audioplayers with USAGE_ALARM works there — if not, use a native MediaPlayer/Ringtone via MethodChannel). Keep the foreground delegation only as an enhancement, not the sole path. At minimum, if no ACK for triggerAlarm within ~1s, fall back to bg-side notification+sound.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: No exact-alarm (AlarmManager) backstop computed from ETA (science-session D2). There is no independent OS-scheduled alarm that fires at the predicted arrival time if the tracking loop/foreground service is dead (Doze, OEM battery kill, process crash, reboot). The only mechanism keeping the alarm alive is the foreground GPS service continuously running for the full journey.
ev: grep across lib/, android/, pubspec.yaml for alarmmanager|exact_alarm|schedule_exact|android_alarm_manager|setExact|zonedSchedule|USE_EXACT returns nothing; manifest declares no SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM/USE_EXACT_ALARM permission (AndroidManifest.xml); pubspec has audioplayers/flutter_local_notifications/vibration/flutter_background_service only. targetSdk=34.
fix: Add android_alarm_manager_plus (or a native AlarmManager.setAlarmClock() via MethodChannel — setAlarmClock is exempt from Doze and shows in the OS alarm UI) plus USE_EXACT_ALARM/SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permissions. On each ETA recompute, (re)schedule an exact alarm for the predicted arrival time minus lead. On fire, the AlarmManager broadcast raises the same notification+sound path independently of the tracking loop. Cancel/reschedule as ETA drifts.

desc: Aggressive OEM battery manager (MIUI/ColorOS/FuntouchOS on cheap Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo/Realme — dominant in India) kills the flutter_background_service foreground isolate while the rider sleeps, because the app is not whitelisted from battery optimization.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION etc. but has NO REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission and no code path requests an exemption (grep for IGNORE_BATTERY/isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations returns nothing). trackingservice.dart:212 sets autoStart:false. Nothing counters OEM background-kill, which on Indian budget phones happens routinely to backgrounded apps.
fix: Foreground service is force-stopped; GPS stream and alarm evaluation stop entirely; the rider is never woken and misses the stop.

desc: Phone battery dies mid-journey (common on cheap phones) and the rider puts it on charge; the phone reboots but the app is not reopened because the rider is asleep.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml has no BOOT_COMPLETED receiver and no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission; trackingservice.dart:212/220 use autoStart:false. Recovery from snapshot at trackingservice.dart:2020-2102 only runs if the OS restarts the background isolate (process death), which does not happen across a full reboot. splash_screen.dart:105-140 restores only when the user opens the app.
fix: Tracking never resumes after reboot; the persisted TrackingSnapshot is only consumed on manual app launch (splash) or OS-driven isolate restart, so no alarm ever fires.

desc: WRONG DIRECTION: rider boards the correct line at the wrong platform and travels away from the destination, underground (no GPS).
ev: trackingservice.dart:1143 soft-lock runs only `if (!isMetroStep)`; trackingservice.dart:1175-1185 uses ekfState.s for metro progress; there is no board-direction validation anywhere in alarm_controller.dart / trackingservice.dart.
fix: On a metro leg the soft-lock/deviation check is skipped and progress = EKF arc-length, which integrates speed magnitude with no signed direction-along-route check. EKF 's' keeps INCREASING as the train moves, so the app 'advances' toward the modeled destination and fires a spurious 'Arriving' alarm while the rider heads the opposite way; the true stop is never reached and no correct alarm ever comes. (On an elevated/GPS section the reverse failure occurs: snapping to the one-directional polyline makes progress DECREASE, so the destination threshold is never crossed and no alarm fires.) Either way the rider misses.

desc: WRONG TRAIN, right platform: two lines share a platform/corridor (e.g. a common trunk before diverging); rider boards the wrong line going the correct general direction.
ev: trackingservice.dart:1120-1143 (metro legs ignore position deviation); progress is EKF arc-length not GPS-matched (trackingservice.dart:1183-1185); reroute is only driven by deviation which is suppressed on metro legs.
fix: Metro leg ignores lateral deviation, so the app never notices the train is geographically off the prefetched polyline. EKF dead-reckons along the WRONG (prefetched) line's arc-length and fires 'N stops before' / destination at the modeled distance, which corresponds to a completely different physical location on the actual line. Rider is woken at the wrong time/place and is on the wrong train.

desc: Rider starts tracking, screen auto-locks, and they fall asleep. On a cheap India-common phone (MIUI/ColorOS/Realme/Samsung) Doze or the OEM memory-killer freezes/kills the foreground Flutter UI isolate while the screen is off.
ev: lib/services/tracking/heartbeat_monitor.dart:22-99 (timeout=4s, checkInterval=2s; on timeout -> TrackingStateStore.setPaused(true); showTrackingPaused(); stop()). Heartbeat is sent every 1s only from the foreground isolate: lib/services/tracking/foreground_bridge.dart:314-327. Comment at trackingservice.dart:499-505 assumes the foreground Dart timer 'continues to run' when merely backgrounded, which does not hold under Doze / aggressive OEM freezing. No WAKE_LOCK / REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml to defend against this.
fix: The UI isolate stops sending its 1s heartbeat. Within 4s the background service's HeartbeatMonitor concludes the app was 'swiped away', sets paused=true, cancels the journey progress notification and shows a 'Tracking paused — Resume to continue' notification, then STOPS monitoring. No alarm evaluation runs again until the sleeping rider manually taps Resume — so the alarm NEVER fires and they sail past their stop.

desc: A tidy rider clears the app from the recents/task-switcher (or a game/other app pushes it out of memory) before dozing off, intending the persistent tracking notification to keep working.
ev: lib/services/tracking/heartbeat_monitor.dart:57-91 treats missing heartbeat as 'foreground gone' and pauses. Resume only happens via user action: NotificationService RESUME_TRACKING handler (notification_service.dart:1482-1540) or resumeFromNotification (trackingservice.dart:1761-1766). There is no auto-resume and no continued alarm evaluation while paused.
fix: Same heartbeat-timeout path: swiping the UI away stops heartbeats, the service flips to paused and shows 'Resume to continue', and self-suspends alarm checking. The rider believes tracking is live (a notification is still visible) but it is a paused notification requiring a manual tap — the wake-up never comes.

desc: Metro rider is asleep; train enters a long tunnel with full GPS blackout and reaches their target stop while still underground before GPS returns.
ev: Alarm eval is invoked ONLY from LocationStreamHandler._handlePositionUpdate on a LocationManager position event (location_stream_handler.dart:268-273 onCheckAlarm). The periodic GPS-check timer _handleGpsCheckTick (location_stream_handler.dart:428-452) does NOT call onCheckAlarm — it only starts sensor fusion via _checkGpsDropout. EKF advances 's' but is read only when a GPS fix triggers _resolveAlarmRouteState (trackingservice.dart:1183 useEkfForAlarmProgress); no timer fires the alarm from EKF alone. Sensor-fusion's fused-position stream (sensor_fusion.dart:220 _positionController.add) has zero consumers — location_stream_handler only subscribes ekfStateStream (line 585). EKF is not wired to fire alarms.
fix: No new Position events arrive, so the alarm is never re-evaluated and never fires until GPS returns after the stop — rider sleeps past their stop (product death).

desc: Long intercity sleeper (6-10h, one stop) that crosses a state boundary, e.g. Bangalore->Chennai, Mumbai->Ahmedabad. Rider tries to set the alarm before boarding.
ev: homescreen.dart:255-306 _validateSameState reverse-geocodes origin+dest and homescreen.dart:289-294 returns false on mismatch; homescreen.dart:607-616 hard-blocks with 'Routes that cross state boundaries are not supported' and returns before startTracking. Most Indian intercity trains are cross-state, so the flagship long-journey case is unsupported. (Only fail-open if geocode errors, homescreen.dart:280/303.)
fix: Journey creation is refused entirely, so the rider never arms an alarm for the exact use case (multi-hour single-stop sleeper) the product is meant for; they fall back to nothing and oversleep.

desc: Rider swipes WakePoint away from the recents/task switcher after setting the alarm and falls asleep (extremely common: people close apps before sleeping). Background foreground-service isolate keeps GPS running, but the UI isolate is killed.
ev: alarm_controller.dart:277-286 delegates all alarm output to foreground; foreground_bridge.dart:203-233 handles it only in UI isolate; heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-99 downgrades to a silent 'paused' notification when the foreground is gone; background isolate deliberately never plays sound ('Background isolate cannot reliably start audio... Always delegate' comment at alarm_controller.dart:278-280).
fix: Alarm is detected in the background isolate but NEVER rung. AlarmController.triggerAlarmNotification() with isBackgroundIsolate==true does ONLY `service.invoke('triggerAlarm', ...)` and returns without showing a notification or playing sound (lib/services/tracking/alarm_controller.dart:277-286). That invoke is handled by ForegroundBridge._handleTriggerAlarm in the DEAD UI isolate (lib/services/tracking/foreground_bridge.dart:203-233), so no sound (AlarmPlayer), no vibration (native channel lives in MainActivity), and no full-screen notification fire. HeartbeatMonitor instead posts a 'tracking paused' notification after a 4s timeout and then STOPS monitoring (lib/services/tracking/heartbeat_monitor.dart:83-91) — a sleeping rider never sees it. Rider sleeps past the stop.

desc: Cheap Indian phone with aggressive OEM battery management (MIUI/Xiaomi, Realme/Oppo/ColorOS, Vivo/Funtouch, Samsung Device Care) silently kills the foreground service during a long sleep ride — the stated India-first target hardware.
ev: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS); permission_service.dart:13-99 requests only location/notification/activityRecognition; trackingservice.dart:206-224 configures autoStart:false with no watchdog/restart.
fix: The app never requests a battery-optimization / autostart exemption. AndroidManifest.xml declares no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission, and PermissionService only asks for location/notification/activity-recognition (lib/services/permission_service.dart:13-26) — never isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations or the OEM autostart whitelist. On these OEMs the foreground service is reaped after screen-off, both isolates die, GPS stops, and no alarm fires. There is no restart mechanism (autoStart:false, trackingservice.dart:212).

desc: The metro line runs through a long underground tunnel (Bangalore purple/green underground stretches) and the rider's trigger point (N stops before, or distance/time-before) falls inside the GPS-dead zone.
ev: location_stream_handler.dart:209-273 (onCheckAlarm only on real GPS ticks); location_stream_handler.dart:428-452 (dropout tick does not check alarms); location_stream_handler.dart:585-592 (EKF state stored but only broadcast, never drives alarm).
fix: Alarm evaluation is frozen during GPS outage. onCheckAlarm is invoked ONLY from _handlePositionUpdate, which fires only when the GPS positionStream emits (lib/services/tracking/location_stream_handler.dart:209-273). The periodic _gpsCheckTimer tick (_handleGpsCheckTick, line 428-452) never calls onCheckAlarm. The EKF/sensor-fusion runs and updates _lastEkfState via onEkfUpdate (line 585-590) but that estimate is NOT fed to the alarm check — matching the stated 'EKF built but not wired into production alarm logic.' So underground the alarm cannot fire until GPS returns, which may be at or past the target stop.

desc: NEW DIMENSION platform-parity/iOS — THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS. The product is 'Flutter Android+iOS', but the entire tracking/alarm architecture is Android-only. On iOS, once the rider locks the screen and sleeps, iOS suspends the app: there is no foreground-service equivalent, the flutter_background_service iOS handler is a no-op, and Info.plist declares NO UIBackgroundModes (no 'location', no 'audio', no 'processing'). So the GPS stream stops, the EKF never runs, the heartbeat monitor's own logic would pause tracking, and the alarm never fires — for 100% of iOS riders, every journey.
ev: ios/Runner/Info.plist has usage-description strings but NO <key>UIBackgroundModes</key> at all (grep confirms 'NO UIBackgroundModes key found'). onIosBackground (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:604-607) just returns true and does nothing. IosConfiguration wired at trackingservice.dart:219-222. All background-survival evidence in the existing enumeration (foreground service, Doze, heartbeat, WAKE_LOCK, OEM killers, BOOT_COMPLETED) is Android-only; the iOS execution model — background location deferral, no long-running compute, ~30s background budget, Background App Refresh being user-disableable, killing background audio when nothing is playing — is never addressed.
fix: Every iOS rider who locks the phone and sleeps (the core use case) gets zero position updates, zero alarm evaluation, and no wake-up. Silent, total, product-death across an entire declared platform — worse than any single Android edge case because it is not an edge case, it is the default path on iOS.

desc: NEW DIMENSION fail-safe/redundancy/dead-man's-switch. There is no independent last-resort backstop: no dumb OS-scheduled local/AlarmManager notification armed for the estimated arrival clock-time that would fire even if the whole tracking isolate is dead (Doze, OEM kill, reboot, iOS suspend, thermal starvation). Every alarm path depends on live position callbacks flowing through one fragile isolate; when that isolate dies for ANY reason there is no plan B, and the sleeping rider is never told tracking stopped.
ev: All firing is position-callback-driven (lib/services/tracking/location_stream_handler.dart:268-273 onCheckAlarm); the periodic timer _handleGpsCheckTick does NOT fire alarms. No use of Android AlarmManager exact-alarm / SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM or a pre-scheduled local notification at estimated arrival time anywhere. No server-side push backstop. No user-facing 'tracking has stopped' alert when the stream goes silent.
fix: Any of the numerous already-catalogued isolate-death causes (heartbeat pause, OEM battery killer, reboot, storage-full snapshot loss, iOS suspend) becomes an unrecoverable silent miss because nothing independent is scheduled to wake the rider. A single scheduled fallback alarm at ETA would convert most CRITICAL misses into a merely-early annoyance.

desc: First-time rider installs on a budget phone (Redmi/Realme, common in India), arms a metro alarm, locks the screen and dozes. Aggressive OS battery optimization (default ON for new apps) freezes/kills the flutter_background_service after some minutes of Doze.
ev: There is NO battery-optimization handling anywhere. Manifest (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) does not declare REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS; grep for isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations/ignoreBatteryOptimizations across lib/ returns nothing. pubspec has battery_plus (reads battery level only) and android_intent_plus but no disable-battery-optimization flow. PermissionService (lib/services/permission_service.dart) requests only location, notification, activityRecognition. Service runs as isForegroundMode:true (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:210) which is necessary but insufficient against OEM Doze without whitelisting.
fix: The foreground tracking service is suspended, GPS/EKF stops updating, and the alarm never fires. Rider sleeps past the stop. This is the exact 'fire late = product death' outcome.

desc: Rider on Xiaomi MIUI / Oppo/Realme ColorOS / Vivo FuntouchOS (the dominant Indian budget stack) where the OEM aggressively kills backgrounded apps and requires a manual 'Autostart' + 'No battery restrictions' toggle buried in a vendor-specific settings screen.
ev: grep for xiaomi|oppo|vivo|oem|autostart|manufacturer across lib/ returns nothing. No onboarding screen exists (grep onboard|tutorial|walkthrough|firstRun|hasSeen returns nothing). SplashScreen (lib/screens/splash_screen.dart) goes straight to init+home with no education. No per-OEM deep-link or guidance is ever presented.
fix: Even with Android-standard permissions granted, the vendor kills the service; the alarm silently never fires. The rider has no idea a hidden OEM toggle exists.

desc: Android 11+ rider grants foreground location at the 'Wake Me' prompt. The app then immediately calls Permission.locationAlways.request() for 'Allow all the time', which on Android 11+ CANNOT be granted inline — the OS either returns while-in-use silently or requires a manual trip to app Settings.
ev: lib/services/permission_service.dart _requestBackgroundLocation() shows a rationale then calls Permission.locationAlways.request() and returns status.isGranted — it never checks isPermanentlyDenied and has NO _showSettingsDialog path (unlike location/notification). homescreen.dart:481-499: on failure the else branch only does setState(_isLoading=false) with the comment 'The service already showed the user a dialog' — which is false for the background-location decline path.
fix: _requestBackgroundLocation returns false, requestEssentialPermissions returns false, canProceed is false, and _onWakeMePressed just resets the loading spinner. The trip never starts and, if the rider tapped through, tracking runs only 'while in use' — dies the moment the screen locks. No Settings guidance is offered for background location.

desc: Core use case: an iOS rider sets a wake-up alarm, locks the phone, and falls asleep on the train. iOS suspends the Flutter app within seconds of screen-lock/backgrounding.
ev: ios/Runner/Info.plist declares NO <key>UIBackgroundModes</key> at all (no 'location', 'audio', or 'processing'). trackingservice.dart:604-607 onIosBackground() is a no-op that just returns true. The alarm is only ever evaluated inside LocationManager().positionStream.listen(...) in location_stream_handler.dart:209 — when iOS suspends the app that stream stops and the loop dies. There is no OS mechanism keeping the app alive.
fix: The suspended app produces zero GPS updates, so the position-stream loop that drives ALL alarm evaluation never runs. The rider sails past their stop and is never woken. Silent, total failure for every iOS rider on the primary journey.

desc: Even a rider whose ETA is roughly known in advance (metro N-minutes-before mode) locks the phone; one might expect a pre-scheduled fallback notification to fire at the target time while suspended.
ev: notification_service.dart uses _notificationsPlugin.show() everywhere (lines 818, 906, 968, 1100, 1202) and never zonedSchedule/periodicallyShow. Alarm origin is triggerAlarm invoked from the live loop (alarm_controller.dart:281, 449, 521, 694, 788). Nothing is scheduled with iOS ahead of time, so suspension = no delivery.
fix: There is no pre-scheduled alarm. All alarms are shown live at the moment of evaluation, so while the app is suspended nothing is queued in iOS's notification scheduler to fire. No wake-up.

desc: iOS rider enters a metro tunnel (the exact case the EKF dead-reckoning was built for) with the phone locked. GPS is lost and the app is already suspended.
ev: SensorFusionManager/EKF is driven from the same background isolate (trackingservice.dart:617 _sensorFusionManager, location_stream_handler.dart:585 ekfStateStream) which iOS suspends. No UIBackgroundModes 'location' or 'processing' in Info.plist means neither Core Location nor a background task keeps the isolate scheduled. NSMotionUsageDescription exists but motion updates are not delivered to a suspended app.
fix: The EKF/sensor-fusion fallback that is supposed to dead-reckon over the known route also never runs, because it too lives in the suspended background isolate and is fed by the same halted position stream. Motion sensor delivery also stops. The one feature meant to save tunnel riders is doubly dead on iOS.

desc: The app requests 'Always' location permission on iOS, the rider grants it, and reasonably believes background tracking now works.
ev: permission_service.dart:60-70 requests Permission.locationAlways and Info.plist has NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription, so the user is prompted for Always. But there is NO AppleSettings/allowBackgroundLocationUpdates anywhere (grep of lib/ returns none — location_manager.dart:45 uses generic LocationSettings) and no UIBackgroundModes 'location'. Background delivery therefore never happens despite the granted permission.
fix: Granting Always-location does nothing without the background-location capability. iOS still stops delivering updates to the suspended app, so the rider gets a false sense of safety, relies on the alarm, and misses the stop. This is worse than an outright denial because it hides the failure.

desc: Suppose a notification somehow fires on iOS while the rider is asleep with a Sleep Focus / Do Not Disturb enabled (typical for someone napping) and the phone on silent.
ev: notification_service.dart:772-774 DarwinNotificationDetails sets presentSound: false and never sets interruptionLevel critical/timeSensitive; DarwinInitializationSettings() at line 563-564 requests no critical-alert permission and there is no ios/*.entitlements file granting com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts. The loud sound comes from AlarmPlayer (alarm_player.dart:20 AVAudioSessionCategory.playback) which needs the app alive and has no UIBackgroundModes 'audio' to start playback while backgrounded.
fix: The delivered notification is silent and non-urgent: it does not bypass Focus/DND, plays no sound, and the loud alarm audio can't start because it requires the app to be running. The rider sleeps through a soundless banner.

desc: OEM battery killer (Xiaomi MIUI, Realme, Oppo, Vivo, Samsung) silently kills the whole flutter_background_service while rider sleeps mid-route. These skins are the dominant install base in India.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml declares the service (line 53-54) with no restart guarantee; trackingservice.dart:212 sets autoStart:false and there is NO android_alarm_manager_plus/workmanager/zonedSchedule anywhere in lib/android (repo-wide grep empty). Nothing independent of the isolate is armed for the arrival time, so when the OS reaps the isolate there is no plan B.
fix: The background isolate is destroyed. All position callbacks stop, alarm evaluation stops, and the alarm never fires. Rider blows past the target stop with zero notification. Product death.

desc: Phone reboots mid-journey (forced OTA update, thermal shutdown, battery dip, kernel panic) while rider sleeps on a long ride.
ev: Manifest has no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and no boot BroadcastReceiver; trackingservice.dart:212/220 both set autoStart:false. The recovery path at trackingservice.dart:2020-2078 (_onStart with null initialData) can only run if something restarts the isolate — after a reboot nothing does. No OS AlarmClock/zonedSchedule survives the reboot to wake the rider.
fix: After reboot the background service never comes back, so the snapshot-based recovery flow is never even reached. Rider sleeps through the stop.

desc: iOS: rider is asleep, screen off, phone stationary on the seat. iOS suspends then terminates the app to reclaim resources (standard iOS background policy for a motionless, backgrounded app).
ev: onIosBackground (trackingservice.dart:604-607) just calls ensureInitialized() and returns true — no BGTaskScheduler/BGAppRefresh registration, and no scheduled UNTimeIntervalNotification/zonedSchedule armed for ETA (repo grep for BGTaskScheduler/zonedSchedule empty). Once iOS suspends the app there is nothing scheduled at the OS level to wake the rider.
fix: The Dart isolate is suspended/killed; no position processing, no alarm. iOS gives no location callbacks to a suspended app parked in a tunnel or sitting still between stops.

desc: Rider swipes the app away from recents (thinking they are just tidying the screen before sleeping), then Doze or memory pressure later kills the surviving background isolate.
ev: HeartbeatMonitor (heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-98) runs inside the background isolate and only watches the FOREGROUND heartbeat; on timeout it calls showTrackingPaused then stop() (line 91). showTrackingPaused (notification_service.dart:1123) issues an ordinary _notificationsPlugin.show — not the full-screen alarm intent — so a sleeping rider will neither hear nor see it, and there is no scheduled fallback if the isolate then dies.
fix: HeartbeatMonitor detects the foreground death and shows a low-key 'Tracking paused' notification, then STOPS monitoring. If the isolate is subsequently killed, the paused notification is stale and no alarm ever fires. Even in the best case the rider only gets a silent passive notification, not a wake-up.

desc: Low-RAM budget phone (2-3 GB, extremely common in India) under memory pressure: Android LowMemoryKiller reaps the tracking service to free RAM for a foregrounded app the rider opened before dozing off.
ev: Same structural gap: single isolate (trackingservice.dart _onStart), no zonedSchedule/AlarmManager backstop, autoStart:false. The in-isolate HeartbeatMonitor cannot help because it dies with the isolate it lives in (heartbeat_monitor.dart:14, constructed at trackingservice.dart:625 in background-isolate scope).
fix: Service killed by LMK exactly like the OEM-killer case; no restart is guaranteed for a foreground service under LMK, and no independent alarm is scheduled, so the rider misses the stop.

desc: A Deaf rider naps with the phone resting flat on the padded metro seat or on their lap (not in a pocket against the body). At the target stop the alarm fires: audio is useless to them, so vibration is their only channel.
ev: lib/services/alarm_haptics.dart uses ONE hardcoded pattern (const [0,500,250,500,250,1000,500], repeat:0) with no amplitude/escalation and no alternate cue; if Vibration.hasVibrator()!=true it silently `return`s (lines 40-44). notification_service.dart _alarmVibrationPattern is the same fixed 3s loop. grep for torch/flashlight/Wearable/flutter_tts across lib/ and android/ returns nothing — there is no flash, LED, wearable, or escalation fallback whatsoever.
fix: The single fixed waveform is absorbed by the soft surface and never reaches the body; the rider feels nothing and sleeps past the stop — product death for this population.

desc: Cheap Indian phone (Xiaomi/MIUI, Realme/Oppo/ColorOS, Vivo/FuntouchOS) with aggressive battery management. Rider starts tracking, pockets the phone, and sleeps. The OS kills the idle foreground service well before the target stop.
ev: grep of lib/ for ignoreBatteryOpt|batteryOptim|autostart|autoStart|Xiaomi|MIUI|OEM|manufacturer finds nothing except an audio-attribute comment in lib/services/alarm_player.dart:80. Permission flow (lib/services/permission_service.dart requestEssentialPermissions) requests only location, notification, activityRecognition — no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, no autostart deep-link. Service is autoStart:false (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:212,220) with no keep-alive re-arm.
fix: Foreground service is silently killed by OEM battery optimization; tracking dies, no alarm ever fires, rider sleeps past the stop and is stranded. The app never requests a battery-optimization exemption, never requests autostart, and shows no OEM-specific guidance — the single largest reliability killer on the India-first target hardware is entirely unmitigated.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Rider sleeps and their intended-stop alarm fails to wake them (dismissed while groggy, DND, or a late GPS fix). The train continues along the SAME correct line to the terminus and then into a depot siding — an unfamiliar, unsafe place late at night.
ev: TrackingTerminationPolicy.shouldTerminate only fires on deviation from route (RULE 1/2/3 all require deviationDistanceKm from route, lib/services/tracking_termination_policy.dart:151-217) and is only invoked inside the reroute/deviation path (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1348-1364). AlarmEventType has finalStation defined (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:12) but no evaluator branch fires an unconditional end-of-line safety wake; alarms are strictly one-per-leg keyed to the target (RULE 1, alarm_evaluator.dart:159).
fix: Riding to the end of the correct line is ON-route, not a deviation, so the termination safety net never engages; and even if it did, it only runs during a reroute/deviation check. There is no 'you have reached the end of the line / final station' backstop alarm independent of the target-stop alarm. The rider is carried into a terminus/depot with no second wake, the worst-case stranding scenario.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Tunnel section (e.g. Bangalore Metro underground stretch) where the target stop is inside or immediately after the tunnel. GPS drops for the tunnel duration.
ev: grep for ekf_orchestrator|EkfOrchestrator|EkfPipeline|degraded_mode|deadReckon across lib/services and lib/screens finds NO reference in the tracking/alarm path (only lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart exists in isolation). Production alarm evaluation (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart) is driven purely by progressMeters from GPS; EKF modules in lib/core/ekf/ are validated only in simulation calibrated to one Bangalore ride, per project brief.
fix: The EKF dead-reckoning that is supposed to carry progress through tunnels is built but NOT wired into the production alarm path, so progressMeters stalls at the last pre-tunnel GPS fix. The stops-before / distance-before threshold is never crossed until GPS returns — by which point the train is past the stop. This is the exact 'silent miss' the product's core value prop claims to solve, and it silently does not exist in production.

desc: WakePoint ships with ZERO OEM-kill mitigation. Verified in code: (1) AndroidManifest.xml (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, lines 3-13) declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION correctly but has NO `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` permission, so the app can never even ask to be Doze/battery-exempt. (2) permission_service.dart requestEssentialPermissions() (lines 13-26) stops after location+notification+activity-recognition; it never requests battery-optimization exemption and never deep-links to any OEM autostart/protected-apps screen. (3) There is no `<queries>` visibility for OEM settings packages, so even a future deep-link cannot resolve on Android 11+. (4) MainActivity.kt has only a vibration MethodChannel; no bridge to launch OEM intents. Net effect: on the aggressive-OEM phones that dominate WakePoint's India-first market (~60-75% of units), the foreground service + its background isolate get frozen or killed within minutes of screen-off because autostart is OFF by default and the app is Doze-throttled — the exact documented #1 cause of dead alarm apps. A sleeping rider on a Redmi/Vivo/Samsung is not woken. This is product death, hence SHOWSTOPPER.
ev: Un-closable gaps remain and MUST be disclosed to the user, not hidden: (1) HUAWEI/HONOR NO-GMS (EMUI/HarmonyOS): PowerGenie kills everything not on its private whitelist with no user-facing exemption; removal needs ADB (adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.huawei.powergenie). No app-side or user-toggle fix exists — WakePoint is fundamentally unreliable here; consider a hard warning or unsupported-device banner. (2) ULTRA/EXTREME BATTERY SAVER (all OEMs): when the user manually enables it, even battery-exempt allow-listed apps get frozen; nothing the app can do. (3) Samsung silently re-adds apps to 'Sleeping apps' after OTA updates and after ~3 days of non-use — mitigated only by the re-nag loop, never permanently. (4) Autostart/protected-apps is a privileged setting: it is IMPOSSIBLE to toggle or even reliably read programmatically on MIUI/HyperOS/ColorOS/FuntouchOS/OriginOS — the app is at the mercy of whether the user actually flips it in the deep-linked screen. (5) android_intent_plus ComponentNames drift across OS versions (HyperOS, ColorOS 15, OriginOS 5); the verbatim strings will silently fail on some builds, hence the try/catch->openAppSettings fallback is mandatory and some users land on a generic settings page. (6) The permission_handler ignoreBatteryOptimizations dialog can return 'denied' even after the user taps Allow on certain OEMs (GitHub #1191), so trust the isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations re-check over the request() return value. Net: even with everything built, a realistic ~10-20% of aggressive-OEM users will not complete or will have the OS override their setup, so the app also needs a defense-in-depth fallback alarm strategy (exact alarms / server-push) outside this area's scope.
fix: MANIFEST: In android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml after line 13 add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS" />`. Also add a `<queries>` block (alongside the existing one at lines 58-63) listing the OEM settings packages you will deep-link so startActivity/resolveActivity works under Android 11+ package-visibility: com.miui.securitycenter, com.coloros.safecenter, com.oppo.safe, com.vivo.permissionmanager, com.iqoo.secure, com.huawei.systemmanager, com.oneplus.security, com.samsung.android.lool, com.transsion.phonemaster.; BATTERY EXEMPTION (programmatic): Extend PermissionService (lib/services/permission_service.dart). Add a new step after _requestActivityRecognitionPermission() at line 23 (call it before returning true at line 25): `if (Platform.isAndroid && !(await Permission.ignoreBatteryOptimizations.isGranted)) { showRationale then await Permission.ignoreBatteryOptimizations.request(); }`. permission_handler ^12.0.0 (already in pubspec) exposes Permission.ignoreBatteryOptimizations which fires ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS. Guard the .request() in try/catch (known back-button crash, GitHub issue Baseflow/flutter-permission-handler #237).

desc: The audible wake-up exists ONLY inside the Flutter background isolate. `AlarmController.checkAndTriggerAlarm` (lib/services/tracking/alarm_controller.dart:298) is the sole path that fires the alarm, and it is driven per-GPS-tick from `_checkAndTriggerAlarm` (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:2171, :2440). The actual sound comes from Dart `AlarmPlayer.playSelected()` inside `NotificationService.showWakeUpAlarm` (lib/services/notification_service.dart:794-826), and the alarm notification channel is deliberately silent (`playSound:false`, notification_service.dart:617/728). So if the isolate is dead — Doze/App Standby, OEM kill (Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo/Samsung on the India-first market), heartbeat_monitor pausing tracking on UI death, or OOM — there is NOTHING scheduled at the OS level to make noise. AlarmReceiver.kt is a 1-line empty file, there is no AlarmManager usage anywhere, no BOOT_COMPLETED receiver, no exact-alarm permission in AndroidManifest.xml, and the manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT but no code ever schedules an OS alarm to post that FSI. A sleeping rider whose process died mid-journey is never woken = product death.
ev: Un-closable / partially-closable gaps: (1) DND — CATEGORY_ALARM + USAGE_ALARM plays on the alarm stream so it is audible under silent/vibrate ringer, but full DND suppression is only bypassed if the user grants notification-policy access (setBypassDnd is best-effort otherwise). A rider in strict DND may not hear the backstop. (2) Aggressive OEMs (Xiaomi MIUI/HyperOS, Oppo/Realme/OnePlus ColorOS, Vivo Funtouch, Transsion) can kill the process AND, on some builds, drop pending AlarmManager alarms when the app is force-stopped by the user or aggressively cleaned; battery-optimization exemption + 'Autostart' allowlisting (dontkillmyapp.com) mitigates but cannot be guaranteed programmatically — needs an onboarding education flow. setAlarmClock survives Doze and normal background but a user-initiated Force Stop cancels all alarms until next app launch (true on all Android). (3) Huawei without GMS: no Play Store FSI grant path and harsher power management; setAlarmClock still works but FSI grant and channel behavior are less predictable — treat HMS devices as best-effort. (4) setExactAndAllowWhileIdle (fallback if setAlarmClock is ever unavailable) is subject to a ~10-minute minimum window between while-idle alarms in deep Doze [HARD FACT], which would blunt fine-grained rescheduling — that is why setAlarmClock is primary. (5) If the process is dead, the backstop notification's sound is the channel default alarm ringtone, NOT the user's custom AlarmPlayer ringtone — acceptable tradeoff for guaranteed audio. (6) The backstop time is only as good as the last computed ETA before the process died; a rider who boards a much faster/slower train than the model right before a kill could be woken early/late by up to the model error — the safetyLead earliness budget absorbs the 'late' direction, which is the only fatal one.
fix: MANIFEST (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml): add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/> (auto-granted normal permission; WakePoint is an alarm app so it passes Play's exact-alarm policy) and <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED"/>. Keep USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT (already line 13). Optionally also add SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM for max-target flexibility, but USE_EXACT_ALARM is sufficient and cannot be revoked by the user.; MANIFEST: register the two receivers inside <application>: <receiver android:name=".AlarmReceiver" android:exported="false"/> and <receiver android:name=".BootReceiver" android:exported="true"><intent-filter><action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"/><action android:name="android.intent.action.MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED"/></intent-filter></receiver>.

desc: The active journey has NO time-based backstop that survives loss of the tracking loop. Every wake path (GPS stream -> EKF -> alarm_evaluator) runs only inside the flutter_background_service Dart isolate. If that isolate dies and is not revived (device reboot, aggressive-OEM kill, low-memory kill without START_STICKY re-delivery), nothing wakes the rider. Confirmed concrete holes: (1) AndroidManifest has NO RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED and the app registers NO boot receiver; AlarmReceiver.kt is a 0-byte empty file (verified) and is not declared in the manifest -> reboot mid-journey is unrecoverable. (2) flutter_background_service is configured autoStart:false with NO autoStartOnBoot (trackingservice.dart:209-224) -> the OS will not relaunch the service after boot. (3) There is NO exact-alarm / AlarmManager backstop anywhere and no android_alarm_manager/workmanager package in pubspec -> the ONLY thing that can fire the alarm is a live position loop; if it is dead, arrival passes silently. (4) HeartbeatMonitor conflates UI-death with a journey PAUSE: on heartbeat timeout it calls TrackingStateStore.setPaused(true), cancels the journey notification, shows a 'paused' notification and stops itself (heartbeat_monitor.dart:83-91) -> when the OEM kills the UI Activity of a sleeping rider, the journey is deliberately halted. (5) There is NO periodic watchdog (WorkManager/JobScheduler) to detect a stalled loop and revive it. Snapshot persistence (tracking_state_store.dart / homescreen.dart:780) is reasonable but stores NO absolute worst-case arrival time, so even a recovered process cannot arm a correct time backstop.
ev: HARD residual (un-closable) gaps remain even after all 9 steps. (1) Manufacturer force-stop / 'App killed' state on aggressive OEMs (Xiaomi MIUI/HyperOS, Oppo/Vivo/Realme ColorOS, Samsung, Huawei EMUI -- see dontkillmyapp.com): a user-initiated force-stop or OEM auto-management can cancel pending AlarmManager alarms AND suppress the BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast until the app is manually opened once. On these devices even setAlarmClock can be dropped; the only mitigations are the battery-optimization + autostart whitelist prompts (step 9), which are user-dependent and frequently ignored. This is the dominant India-first risk and cannot be fully closed in software. (2) Huawei devices without GMS are unaffected by the GMS-related paths but STILL honor AlarmManager/boot receivers -- so LAYER 0/1 work there; the residual is only their especially aggressive PowerGenie killing. (3) WorkManager's 15-minute floor means a stalled loop can go undetected for up to ~15 min, and under Doze the worker may be deferred further -- acceptable only because LAYER 0 (exact alarm) is independent of it. (4) iOS has NO guaranteed background execution or service restart; if the user force-quits (swipe up) the app, background location stops and only the pre-scheduled local notification remains -- and that notification is a plain alert, not the full tracking experience, and cannot be dynamically retimed while the app is dead. (5) Clock/timezone changes and very-early actual arrival (rider arrives far faster than worst-case) mean the time backstop must be armed pessimistically and continuously pushed later by the live loop; if the live loop dies early, the rider may be woken meaningfully before the stop -- an accepted trade (early is survivable, late is death). (6) SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM can be revoked by the user or by Play policy review of USE_EXACT_ALARM; add runtime canScheduleExactAlarms() checks and a degraded inexact-alarm fallback, accepting Doze-induced imprecision.
fix: 1. NATIVE EXACT-ALARM BACKSTOP (highest priority, single biggest risk-reducer). Add to AndroidManifest.xml (after line 13): <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/> and <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"/> (fallback for pre-14 / Play-policy rejection). Implement the empty android/app/src/main/java/com/example/geowake2/AlarmReceiver.kt as a BroadcastReceiver whose onReceive() launches a native full-screen alarm Activity (FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK, setShowWhenLocked/turnScreenOn) and starts the ringtone+vibration WITHOUT requiring the Flutter engine. Declare it in the manifest: <receiver android:name=".AlarmReceiver" android:exported="false"/>. Add an ExactAlarmScheduler (Kotlin) exposing schedule(epochMs, payload)/cancel() via AlarmManager.setAlarmClock(AlarmClockInfo(epochMs, showIntent), pendingIntent).; 2. WIRE FLUTTER->NATIVE. In MainActivity.kt (extend configureFlutterEngine ~line 25) add MethodChannel 'geowake/exact_alarm' with methods armBackstop(epochMs, destinationName), cancelBackstop(), canScheduleExact(). Create lib/services/tracking/exact_alarm_backstop.dart wrapping that channel. Call armBackstop from startTracking (trackingservice.dart:302 area) right after the service ack, and cancelBackstop from completeEndTracking (trackingservice.dart:516) and _handleStopAlarm.

desc: As built, the EKF is fed the accelerometer/gyro at the sensors_plus DEFAULT rate of 5 Hz, not the >=50 Hz dead-reckoning needs, and iOS delivers nothing at all once the screen locks. In production, lib/services/tracking/location_stream_handler.dart:562-571 constructs SensorFusionManager with accelerometerStream:null / gyroscopeStream:null, so lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart:184 and :255 fall back to the deprecated top-level accelerometerEvents / gyroscopeEvents getters, which use SensorInterval.normalInterval = 200 ms = 5 Hz (confirmed in plus_plugins source: normalInterval = Duration(milliseconds: 200); gameInterval = Duration(milliseconds: 20)). No samplingPeriod / SensorInterval.gameInterval is requested anywhere, so the manifest's HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS permission is dead weight (that permission only gates >200 Hz on Android 12+; 50 Hz never needed it). The task premise that there is NO wakelock is only half true: flutter_background_service_android's BackgroundService.runService() unconditionally acquires a static PowerManager.PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK (LOCK_NAME = BackgroundService.class.getName()+'.Lock'), so on Android the CPU does NOT suspend while the foreground service runs and non-wake-up accel/gyro DO deliver with the screen off. So the Android problem is not delivery, it is RATE (5 Hz) plus the OEM-kill risk that releases that plugin wakelock. On iOS the problem is fatal: Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes, so CoreMotion (which sensors_plus uses via CMMotionManager) has no background mode to ride on and stops delivering the instant the app is suspended on screen lock. Net: DR as currently wired cannot survive a real screen-off metro ride on either platform, which means late alarms = product death.
ev: Even with every step applied, background IMU is NOT guaranteed on the India-dominant aggressive-OEM Android fleet. (1) MIUI/ColorOS/Funtouch/HyperOS can kill the foreground service despite a battery-optimization exemption; when the FGS dies, the plugin's PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK is released and accel/gyro delivery stops mid-ride (dontkillmyapp documents that background/foreground work 'simply does not work right' on MIUI even with system battery optimization disabled). This gap is only mitigated by autostart/lock-in-recents user guidance, never fully closed. (2) Full Doze is less of a threat during an actual ride because motion resets the Doze idle timer, but a rider sitting perfectly still in a stopped train + screen off could still let an OEM tighten throttling. (3) iOS: if the user grants only 'While Using' (not 'Always') location, or the location background mode is not continuously active, the app suspends on lock and CMMotionManager stops — DR is dead and only the GPS+schedule floor saves the rider; CMSensorRecorder is NOT a real-time rescue (accelerometer-only, no gyro, retrospective batched history you read after the fact, so it cannot feed a live 6-DOF EKF or wake anyone in real time). (4) Huawei-without-GMS is actually FINE for sensors (FGS + wakelock are AOSP, not GMS-dependent) even though its GPS/push story is broken — so the IMU risk there is lower than the location/notification risk. CONCLUSION: treat DR as an accuracy enhancer over a GPS+schedule+barometer alarm floor; do not let the product's wake guarantee depend on background IMU being continuously available.
fix: MEASURE FIRST (one metro ride, before trusting DR): in lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart startFusion(), add a debug instrument that increments _accelCount on every accelerometer event and _gyroCount on every gyro event, and every ~10 s of wall-clock (checked inside the accel callback via DateTime.now()) appends one line to a file through the existing ekf_logger/app_logger: {wallClockISO, accelCount, gyroCount, screenOn?}. Run: start tracking, LOCK the screen, ride the metro 15 min, unlock, pull the log. Effective Hz per bucket = count/elapsed. Look for buckets at ~500 accel/10 s (=50 Hz) vs ~50 (=5 Hz today) and for ZERO buckets (= FGS killed / CPU suspended). Run it on a Pixel/Samsung AND a Redmi/Realme (India-representative), each with battery-optimization exemption ON and OFF. This single ride decides whether DR is viable.; RAISE THE RATE: lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart:183-184 replace `(accelerometerStream ?? accelerometerEvents)` with `(accelerometerStream ?? accelerometerEventStream(samplingPeriod: SensorInterval.gameInterval))`; :255 replace `gyroscopeStream ?? gyroscopeEvents` with `gyroscopeStream ?? gyroscopeEventStream(samplingPeriod: SensorInterval.gameInterval)`. Import stays sensors_plus. This is the single change that turns 5 Hz into 50 Hz. (Optionally pass explicit high-rate streams from location_stream_handler.dart:562-571 instead of null so the non-test path is explicit.)

desc: There is no wake guarantee that is independent of the live GPS/EKF tracking loop. Every alarm in production is fired from inside the flutter_background_service isolate (alarm_controller.dart) which only runs while that isolate is alive. If the isolate dies (process kill, OEM task-kill, or an Android 14+ SecurityException when the location-typed foreground service is restarted from the background/boot) nothing fires. Boot recovery today is only the plugin's own BootReceiver, which (a) is armed but restarts a location-typed FGS that is ILLEGAL to start from BOOT_COMPLETED on Android 14+ (targetSdk=34) and throws SecurityException, and (b) even when legal, re-enters GPS tracking with a cold fix so the rider can pass the stop before a fix arrives. AlarmReceiver.kt is empty (0 bytes), there is no exact-alarm backstop, no absolute predicted-arrival timestamp in the snapshot, and AlarmController fired-state is in-memory only so it is lost on every restart. Net: the exact failure mode in the brief — board, sleep, reboot or kill, no wake — is currently real.
ev: Un-closable on Android by any API: (1) Force-stop / aggressive OEM task-kill — a force-stopped app has its AlarmManager alarms cancelled AND its BOOT_COMPLETED/other receivers disabled until the user manually launches the app again, so the backstop and boot receiver are both dead. This is the dominant India-market risk (cheap Xiaomi HyperOS/MIUI, Realme/Oppo/Vivo ColorOS, Samsung). Mitigation is onboarding-only: battery-opt exemption + OEM auto-start/protected-app allowlisting (dontkillmyapp.com); it cannot be guaranteed programmatically. (2) Huawei without GMS: AlarmManager.setAlarmClock is AOSP so the backstop still works natively, but PowerGenie will kill boot/watchdog paths unless the app is on Huawei's protected list. (3) Pre-unlock reboot: credential-encrypted SharedPreferences are unavailable until first unlock, so the backstop cannot be re-armed until the rider unlocks once (unless device-encrypted storage is added). (4) setAndAllowWhileIdle-based plugin watchdog is Doze-throttled to ~9 min on Android 13+ — mitigated because setAlarmClock is Doze-exempt. (5) iOS: user force-quit and app suspension mean only region monitoring / coarse local notifications can wake the app; no exact-time guarantee. The backstop closes the reboot and clean-process-death cases; it does NOT close deliberate force-stop.
fix: P0 Manifest: in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/> (Android 13+, grantable without a prompt for alarm-clock-category apps) and <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"/> (Android 12). Register the app receiver: <receiver android:name=".AlarmReceiver" android:exported="false"/> and (P1) <receiver android:name=".WakeBootReceiver" android:exported="true" android:directBootAware="false"><intent-filter><action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"/><action android:name="android.intent.action.MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED"/><action android:name="android.intent.action.QUICKBOOT_POWERON"/></intent-filter></receiver>.; P0 Native scheduler: create android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/geowake2/ExactAlarmScheduler.kt exposing schedule(triggerAtEpochMs, payloadJson) using AlarmManager.setAlarmClock(AlarmManager.AlarmClockInfo(triggerAt, showIntent), operationPendingIntent->AlarmReceiver) and cancel(). Wire a MethodChannel 'geowake/exact_alarm' in MainActivity.configureFlutterEngine (alongside the existing geowake/alarm_haptics channel) with methods schedule/cancel/canScheduleExact.

desc: WakePoint's entire wake guarantee currently lives inside one fragile place: the Flutter background isolate's per-GPS-tick loop (trackingservice.dart -> AlarmController -> Dart AlarmPlayer on a deliberately SILENT notification channel). Every one of the five failure surfaces converges on that single point: (1) On the aggressive-OEM phones that are 60-75% of the India market the foreground service + isolate get frozen/killed within minutes of screen-off because there is NO battery-optimization exemption request, NO OEM autostart deep-link, and only a PROCESS_TEXT <queries> block. (2) There is NO OS-level alarm: AlarmReceiver.kt is empty, no AlarmManager usage, no USE_EXACT_ALARM permission, so a dead isolate = silent phone. (3) There is NO boot recovery: no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED receiver, so a mid-trip reboot ends tracking permanently. (4) heartbeat_monitor pauses/stops tracking on UI death, actively tearing down the only live layer. (5) The IMU/EKF that is supposed to dead-reckon through tunnels runs at the sensors_plus default 5 Hz (not >=50 Hz) and onGpsUnavailable is never called in production, so the EKF never enters degraded mode and its ETA goes stale exactly at tunnel entry. (6) iOS is entirely non-functional in background (no UIBackgroundModes; plain LocationSettings not AppleSettings) and structurally cannot dead-reckon through a tunnel at all. Net: a sleeping rider whose process is throttled, killed, or rebooted is never woken = product death.
ev: Even fully built, honest un-closable gaps remain and MUST be disclosed in-app, not hidden. ANDROID: (1) Huawei/Honor no-GMS PowerGenie kills everything off its private whitelist with no user toggle (removal needs ADB) - treat as unsupported with a hard warning. (2) User-initiated Force Stop cancels all pending AlarmManager alarms until next launch on every Android - unrecoverable while stopped, but the re-nag/foreground re-arm catches it on next open. (3) Manual Ultra/Extreme battery saver freezes even allow-listed apps. (4) Strict DND can suppress the backstop sound unless the user grants notification-policy access (setBypassDnd is best-effort; USAGE_ALARM is audible under silent/vibrate but not guaranteed under full DND). (5) OEM autostart ComponentNames drift across HyperOS/ColorOS 15/OriginOS 5 - the try/catch->openAppSettings fallback lands some users on a generic page. (6) ~10-20% of aggressive-OEM users won't complete or will have the OS silently override setup (Samsung re-adds to Sleeping apps after OTA/3-day idle) - this is precisely why the OS belt exists as the net. IOS: (7) True deep-tunnel dead-reckoning is impossible - no background CoreMotion; the wake degrades to 'last good ETA snapshot at tunnel entry, fired as a fixed-time AlarmKit alarm', so accuracy is bounded by ETA-prediction quality on the final tunnel segment (safetyLead earliness absorbs the only fatal direction). (8) AlarmKit is iOS 26+ only; older/cheaper Indian iPhones fall to the dismissible Time-Sensitive fallback that doesn't bypass the ring switch. GLOBAL: (9) The belt is only as fresh as the last ETA before the process died; a rider boarding a much faster train right before a kill could be woken early - acceptable, since early is harmless and the safetyLead budget is spent on the late (fatal) side.
fix: MUST-BUILD #1 (Android manifest foundation, ~30 min, unblocks belt+OEM+boot): In android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml add uses-permissions REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, USE_EXACT_ALARM, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, WAKE_LOCK. Register two receivers in <application>: .AlarmReceiver (exported=false) and .BootReceiver (exported=true, intent-filter BOOT_COMPLETED + MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED). Add a second <queries> block (the existing one only lists PROCESS_TEXT) enumerating the OEM settings packages: com.miui.securitycenter, com.coloros.safecenter, com.oppo.safe, com.vivo.permissionmanager, com.iqoo.secure, com.huawei.systemmanager, com.oneplus.security, com.samsung.android.lool, com.transsion.phonemaster. NOTE the native package is com.example.geowake2 (kotlin dir), so receiver names resolve there.; MUST-BUILD #2 (self-sounding backstop channel + real AlarmReceiver, ~1 day, closes the fatal gap for a live-but-dozed OR dead process): In MainActivity.kt (android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/geowake2/MainActivity.kt) createNotificationChannel add channel geowake_backstop_alarm IMPORTANCE_HIGH with sound=RingtoneManager.getDefaultUri(TYPE_ALARM) + AudioAttributes(USAGE_ALARM, CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION), setBypassDnd(true) best-effort, VISIBILITY_PUBLIC. Replace the empty AlarmReceiver.kt (android/app/src/main/java/com/example/geowake2/AlarmReceiver.kt) with an onReceive that posts a notification on that channel: setCategory(CATEGORY_ALARM), setFullScreenIntent(MainActivity PI, true) [MainActivity already has showWhenLocked+turnScreenOn in manifest], setOngoing+insistent, short 1-2s WakeLock, and no-op if an alarm-fired file flag is set.

area: Adversarial stress test of WakePoint's 5-layer rel
desc: The architecture is directionally correct (move the guarantee into an OS setAlarmClock belt + boot recovery + OEM onboarding) and I verified every premise it rests on is true in the repo: AndroidManifest.xml has no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS / USE_EXACT_ALARM / RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED / WAKE_LOCK, no .AlarmReceiver or .BootReceiver registered, and only a PROCESS_TEXT queries block; android/app/src/main/java/com/example/geowake2/AlarmReceiver.kt is genuinely empty (0 bytes); sensor_fusion.dart:184,255 subscribes to the default accelerometerEvents/gyroscopeEvents getters (NOT SensorInterval.gameInterval), so IMU is ~5 Hz; heartbeat_monitor.dart (~L54-90) on UI-death sets paused=true, cancels the journey notification and calls stop() — it actively tears down the live layer; Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes. BUT the plan under-states or leaves open five residual gaps that still kill a sleeping rider even when every layer is built and fires perfectly: (1) THE FATAL DIRECTION IS MIS-FRAMED. residual_risk item (9) claims the only stale-ETA failure is 'woken early (harmless)'. The opposite is the killer: if the process dies during a SLOW segment (crawl/dwell/congestion inflates the ETA), then the train runs fast/express, the frozen setAlarmClock epoch lands AFTER real arrival and the belt fires LATE — the one fatal direction — and a fixed 60-90s safetyLead cannot absorb a multi-minute model error. The belt defeats process-death but NOT ETA-staleness; those are different threats and only the first is solved. (2) DND/BEDTIME: the belt's noise is a notification-channel sound, and the target user is asleep, i.e. maximally likely to have DND/Bedtime on; whether a third-party USAGE_ALARM channel sound survives full DND is OEM-dependent and unverified, and setBypassDnd needs ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY which the plan never requests. (3) FORCE-STOP/SWIPE: setAlarmClock survives lmkd/Doze kills but is CANCELLED by force-stop, and on MIUI/aggressive OEMs a recents-swipe is a force-stop — so Layer 2's 'survives isolate death' is false for the most common user gesture, and boot recovery cannot help without a reboot. (4) iOS AlarmKit fires LATE (documented ~20s to 4+ min on locked devices, worse under the plan's dense per-tick re-scheduling), and the region-relaunch backstop cannot fire in a signal-dead tunnel. (5) Thermal shutdown / dead battery powers the phone off = no layer fires at all.
ev: Even after ALL the above, un-closable remainders that MUST be disclosed in-app: (1) User Force Stop / recents-swipe on force-stop-happy OEMs cancels the belt with no reboot to trigger recovery — a sleeping rider will not relaunch; only next-open re-nag helps, i.e. it protects the NEXT trip, not the current one. (2) Full DND / Total Silence can still suppress a third-party notification-channel sound on some OEMs even with policy access; the true system alarm stream is not reachable from a killed BroadcastReceiver via any public API. (3) Thermal shutdown or dead battery = phone off = zero layers fire; India-summer + cheap phone + 2h GPS+IMU is a real trigger. (4) Huawei/Honor no-GMS PowerGenie remains effectively unsupported. (5) iOS deep-tunnel is structurally a last-good-ETA snapshot: AlarmKit's documented ~4-min lateness on locked devices plus fastest-case bias means iOS wakes early-but-imprecise, and the region backstop is blind underground until the train surfaces at/near the platform. (6) Ultra/Extreme battery saver freezes even exempted apps, killing the live layer early — survivable ONLY because the belt is now fastest-case-biased. (7) USE_EXACT_ALARM Play-policy rejection for an indie forces the user-revocable SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM path, silently downgrading belt exactness. (8) ~10-20% of aggressive-OEM users never complete or get silently re-restricted (Samsung OTA re-sleep, MIUI re-lock). Net after fixes: ~97-99% near-AOSP, ~88-93% aggressive-OEM-with-setup, and an honest 'not guaranteed, use a second alarm' tier for Huawei-no-GMS / DND-total-silence / iOS<26.
fix: FIX R1 (fatal direction) in lib/services/trackingservice.dart around _checkAndTriggerAlarm (line 1213) and the ETA fields (_smoothedETA:621, _apiEtaSeconds:623): do NOT arm backstopEpoch = now + (etaToDestination - lead). Use backstopEpoch = now + (remainingDistanceMeters / V_MAX_LINE) - thresholdLead, with V_MAX_LINE from route metadata (line top speed ~22 m/s) NOT the EtaEngine 9.2 m/s average, so a frozen epoch after process death is EARLY-biased. Add a unit test (alongside test/eta_engine_test.dart) asserting fastest-case epoch <= mean-ETA epoch for a slow-then-fast profile.; Make the spatial trigger PRIMARY: add an Android geofence (play-services Geofencing or native LocationManager proximity alert) at the wake radius, registered via the new MethodChannel, targeting the same AlarmReceiver.kt. Wake on first-to-fire of geofence OR fastest-case time-belt; on iOS the CLCircularRegion becomes co-primary. Position cannot go stale with speed; time can.

desc: Android 11+ background (always) location cannot be granted from an in-app dialog — permission_service calls Permission.locationAlways.request() directly, which silently no-ops on Android 11+; there is no redirect to system settings for the upgrade, so many users stay on 'while in use' and the background service loses fixes in Doze.
ev: permission_service.dart L59-72: _requestBackgroundLocation shows a rationale dialog then calls Permission.locationAlways.request() (L70) and returns its status. No _showSettingsDialog / AppSettings redirect on the always path (that redirect only exists for permanently-denied foreground at L34).
fix: On Android 11+, after granting whenInUse, route the user to app settings (AppSettings.openAppSettings or ACTION_LOCATION_SOURCE) with instructions to pick 'Allow all the time', and verify Permission.locationAlways.isGranted on resume before allowing a trip to start.

desc: No exact-alarm capability and no scheduled fallback — the alarm is a live notification from the foreground service only. If the service dies, nothing re-fires. SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM/USE_EXACT_ALARM and RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED are absent, so there is no time-based safety net and no recovery after an OEM kill or reboot.
ev: grep for EXACT_ALARM/RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED/BOOT across android/ and lib/ returned nothing. notification_service.dart has no zonedSchedule/AndroidScheduleMode/exactAllowWhileIdle (grep empty); only live .show() with fullScreenIntent (L729). No <receiver> in AndroidManifest.xml.
fix: Add USE_EXACT_ALARM/SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM plus a zonedSchedule exactAllowWhileIdle notification as an ETA-based backstop, and a RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED receiver to reschedule after reboot, so a late/killed service still triggers a worst-case alarm.

desc: D8 CONFIRMED: No route versioning, expiry, or service-change/staleness validation of route correctness. The only 'staleness' mechanism is a 5-min cost-oriented TTL on the client Hive cache (route_cache.dart:62) and server NodeCache (config.js:33). Once a route is fetched at journey start it is held in memory and trusted verbatim for the entire (up to 2h) trip. There is no route version field, no schedule/timetable check, no first/last-train awareness (the closed-metro fallback anchors to a hard-coded 09:00, direction_service.dart:130-138), and no re-fetch/re-validation mid-journey. A route planned pre-midnight for a line that stops running, a diverted/suspended line, or a station skipped for maintenance is never detected.
ev: route_cache.dart:62 (defaultTtl 5min), config/config.js:33 (server 5min), direction_service.dart:130-138 & 223-233 (hard-coded 09:00 anchor), route_session_manager.dart:123 registers once; no version/expiry field anywhere (grep for version/stale/expiry/serviceChange found none in the route pipeline).
fix: Stamp each RouteCacheEntry/RouteEntry with a fetch timestamp + planned departure window and a schema version; on session start (and on app-foreground) reject/refresh routes older than a service-relevant threshold; when transit, capture Google's per-step departure_time/arrival_time and warn/terminate if wall-clock has drifted past the planned last-service window.

desc: No wrong-route / wrong-direction / wrong-train detection. Correctness relies solely on geometric lateral deviation: snap offset >150 m sustained -> reroute, 100-150 m -> local switch (route_session_manager.dart:1114-1130). A rider who boards the SAME line in the opposite direction, or a parallel line sharing track/corridor, stays within a few metres of the polyline so no deviation fires. Worse, the snap engine adds a +100 'hard resistance to backward movement' penalty (snap_to_route.dart:171-173) and ActiveRouteManager._headingAgreement ignores real user heading (returns a nominal 0.5 and only checks progress monotonicity, active_route_manager.dart:273-283). So a wrong-direction train freezes progress rather than raising an alarm -- the rider is carried away silently and the 'N stops prior' / arrival alarm simply never approaches.
ev: snap_to_route.dart:171-173 (backward penalty), active_route_manager.dart:273-283 (heading agreement stubbed to 0.5, no compass), route_session_manager.dart:1114-1130 (only lateral-offset bands drive switch/reroute); MetroStopService.validateMetroRoute (metro_stop_service.dart:99) runs only ONCE at journey start (homescreen.dart:565) and only checks the destination is near a stop.
fix: Add a direction-of-travel check: compare user heading / progress trend against the expected boarding->alighting bearing of the active transit leg; if progress is monotonically decreasing or heading opposes the leg for a sustained window while snapped on-route, raise a 'wrong direction / wrong train' alert instead of silently freezing progress.

desc: OSM-only stop enhancement silently UNDERCOUNTS stops when bundled station data is incomplete, corrupting stops-mode 'N stops prior' alarms. enhanceTransitLegStopsWithOsm ignores Google num_stops entirely and sets numStops = count of OSM stations matched within 500 m (transfer_utils.dart:1234-1372). If a line's stations are missing from the ~875-stop bundled file (national coverage is thin outside Delhi; 84 stops even lack a status field), the leg reports fewer intermediate stops than reality, so a 'wake me 2 stops before' alarm is computed against the wrong denominator and can fire late or at the wrong station. Full miss (zero matches) keeps the interpolated fallback, but PARTIAL coverage produces a plausible-but-wrong count with no warning.
ev: transfer_utils.dart:1349-1368 (actualNumStops = intermediateStops.length, 'Use OSM count, not API count'), 1234-1247 (only zero-match keeps original), all_india_stops.dart header (generated static file), stop counts: delhi 311 vs chennai 43 / pune 29 / kochi 25 etc.; refreshed only via app release.
fix: Cross-check OSM-derived stop count against Google num_stops; if they diverge beyond a tolerance, fall back to the API count (or flag low-confidence) rather than trusting OSM blindly; add per-city coverage metadata so incomplete cities degrade to interpolation instead of silently undercounting.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: EKF velocity (EKF.v) is completely unused in the fire/ETA path; ETA speed comes from smoothed GPS speed, which in a metro tunnel (frozen/stale GPS on a Xiaomi/Samsung with screen off) collapses toward 0 or garbage.
ev: currentSpeed = context.smoothedSpeed (EtaEngine smoothed gps.speed, eta_engine.dart:369-370) with raw gps.speed fallback (alarm_controller.dart:580-582). No consumer of ekfState.v exists (grep empty). Metro time-mode ETA then leans on the scheduled step-duration fallback (eta_engine.dart:393-404, alarm_evaluator.dart:1303-1401) rather than the fused velocity the EKF was built to provide.
fix: Use EKF.v (and EKF.mode) as the primary speed input for estimateEtaSecondsToMeters/computeEta when mode==metro||degraded, falling back to GPS speed only in surface mode.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: Metro stop-counting fire has zero position-error tolerance: a single EKF.s error larger than one inter-station spacing mis-counts by a full station, firing a stop late (product-killing) with no guard.
ev: Stop count is a hard threshold on progressMeters vs dedupedStopMeters (alarm_evaluator.dart:776-797); progressMeters=EKF.s on metro legs (trackingservice.dart:1183-1184). No sigmaS band, no hysteresis, no 'fire at N+0.5 stops' cushion.
fix: Add a position-uncertainty cushion (count a stop as 'reached' when progress+z*sigmaS >= stopMeters) and/or fire when remainingStops <= N with a distance-into-approach guard so a late EKF correction cannot skip the trigger.

desc: Time-mode alarm has no real-time or express-train correction: ETA is from Google's planned durations / a synthetic metro dwell model, so a train that is faster than planned (express skipping stops, or simply less dwell) makes the time-before-arrival alarm fire LATE.
ev: No express/schedule/delay/real-time awareness exists (grep for express|skip.*stop|scheduled|delay|arrival_time in lib/ returns only unrelated hits and eta_engine.dart:26 'Metro scheduled model constants' — a synthetic model, not live data). Time-mode targets are computed from step durations and this synthetic model in alarm_evaluator.dart / eta_engine.dart, never reconciled against actual observed speed of THIS train vs the planned local. An express covers the planned distance in less time, so a '5 min before arrival' alarm computed off planned duration triggers after the rider has already passed the stop. Stops-mode degrades more gracefully because it counts stops by geographic meters passed (transfer_utils.dart:157-172 stopsPassed via stopMeters), which still increments as the express physically passes each stop location.
fix: For time-mode, continuously re-estimate ETA from observed along-track speed (already have EKF v and smoothedSpeed) rather than trusting planned durations, and/or steer riders toward stops-mode/distance-mode for transit. At minimum warn that time-mode is unreliable on express services.
