desc: Mid-journey reroute is fully suppressed offline (metro tunnels) AND is effectively inert on metro legs, so the deviation/reroute machinery mainly protects road/walk legs — exactly the opposite of the sleeping-metro-rider use case.
ev: reroute_policy.dart:39-52 returns a no-reroute decision whenever `!_online`, logging 'Reroute Skipped: offline'; trackingservice.dart:1368-1376 independently aborts the fetch when `offlineCoordinator.isOffline`. During a 2h tunnel-heavy metro journey the device is offline for long stretches, so reroute never runs. Separately, metro deviation is nearly undetectable because progress is EKF-clamped and the rider stays laterally on the shared corridor, so DeviationMonitor offset stays low. There is also an explicit un-implemented path for non-metro deviation at trackingservice.dart:1169 ('TODO: Trigger actual reroute if DeviationMonitor doesn't pick this up'). The online/offline signal that gates ReroutePolicy is only pushed from the foreground HomeScreen connectivity listener (homescreen.dart:78-93 -> TrackingService.setOnline at :2444-2446); with the screen off / app backgrounded for hours, that listener's isolate may not deliver events, leaving `_online` stale.
fix: Drive ReroutePolicy connectivity from the background tracking isolate / OfflineCoordinator stream, not the UI screen. Define an explicit offline-deviation behavior (queue a reroute for when connectivity returns, or fall back to a purely geographic destination alarm) instead of silently skipping. Close the trackingservice.dart:1169 TODO for non-metro legs.

desc: No boot / kill recovery to restart tracking autonomously (D2 confirmed). AlarmReceiver.kt is a 0-byte dead file, there is no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and no <receiver> declared. autoStart:false means the service only ever starts from an explicit startTracking() in the running app.
ev: AlarmReceiver.kt is 0 bytes (wc -l = 0). AndroidManifest.xml contains no <receiver> element and no BOOT permission (grep 'receiver|boot' = NONE). trackingservice.dart:212 and :220 set autoStart:false. If the OEM kills the process mid-journey (or the phone reboots), nothing re-launches the foreground service; the only recovery is Android's own service-restart calling _onStart with null data (trackingservice.dart:2020-2102), which aggressive OEMs frequently suppress.
fix: Either accept OS restart-only recovery and document it, or add a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver + a periodic WorkManager watchdog that checks TrackingStateStore.isActive() and restarts the foreground service if a session should be running. Delete the dead AlarmReceiver.kt or wire it up.

desc: No wake-lock is ever held (D1 confirmed). Between GPS callbacks the CPU can sleep in Doze, so the 1 Hz timers (heartbeat, gpsCheck) and alarm evaluation are not guaranteed to run on time when screen-off.
ev: grep for WAKE_LOCK/WakeLock/PowerManager/partial_wake across android/ and lib/ returns zero hits; pubspec.yaml has no wakelock/wakelock_plus dependency. The design relies entirely on the foreground-service + location updates keeping the CPU awake, which is not guaranteed under Doze/app-standby on aggressive OEMs.
fix: Acquire a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK for the duration of an active tracking session (native side in the foreground service), or request a high-accuracy location interval that the OS honors as a wake reason. At minimum hold a wake lock around alarm firing so the sound/vibration path completes.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: HeartbeatMonitor responds to foreground-isolate death by PAUSING tracking (shows a 'Tracking paused' notification and stops monitoring) instead of arming a self-contained alarm — actively converting the exact target scenario (UI killed, screen off) into a silent paused state. The user sees 'Tracking paused' and is never woken.
ev: lib/services/tracking/heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-91 — on heartbeat timeout (4s) it sets paused=true, cancels journey progress, shows showTrackingPaused, then stop()s the monitor. Foreground heartbeats are sent from the UI isolate every 1s (foreground_bridge.dart:314-338), so UI death reliably trips this within ~4s. The bg alarm loop keeps evaluating (no paused gate on _checkAndTriggerAlarm / onCheckAlarm in location_stream_handler.dart:270), so it will still try to fire — but only via the dead-foreground delegation, so still silent.
fix: On heartbeat timeout, do NOT pause; instead switch the alarm-raise path to bg-self-contained mode (post notification + play sound from bg) and/or ensure the exact-alarm backstop is armed. Pausing on UI death is the opposite of the product requirement.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: Android 14 full-screen-intent is not guaranteed and there is no runtime handling. USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is declared but on targetSdk 34 it is restricted for non-calling/alarm-clock apps; there is no canUseFullScreenIntent() check, no special-access request flow, and no fallback if the FSI is downgraded to a mere heads-up notification — meaning the screen may not turn on.
ev: notification_service.dart:729 sets fullScreenIntent:true; manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and android:showWhenLocked/turnScreenOn on MainActivity; targetSdk=34 (android/app/build.gradle:21). grep for canUseFullScreenIntent|requestFullScreenIntent returns nothing — no runtime verification or user prompt to grant the special access.
fix: Check NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent() at setup; if false, route the user to the ACTION_MANAGE_APP_USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT settings screen during onboarding. Because the app's core function is an alarm, it qualifies to hold the permission, but it must be requested/verified. Pair with the exact-alarm backstop as defense-in-depth for screen-wake.

desc: Budget Android phone with NO gyroscope (very common < ₹12k tier) enters a metro tunnel; GPS drops and the EKF dead-reckoning fallback must carry progress.
ev: sensor_fusion.dart:255-267 subscribes to gyroscopeEvents with handleError/cancelOnError; sensor_fusion.dart:229-231 substitutes gx=gy=gz=0.0 when _lastGyro is null. ekf_orchestrator.dart:554-558 computes gyroVariance from those zeros, feeding TiltFilter (line 118-119), ZUPT (357-361), and the σ≤60m degraded snap gate (449-452) that then cannot confirm.
fix: gyroscopeEvents never emits (or errors and is cancelled), so gyro is treated as identically zero; TiltFilter orientation and MotionClassifier gyro features degrade, ZUPT/station-association confidence gates rarely pass, so DR drifts and station snaps are rejected — no reliable progress underground.

desc: Very noisy cheap accelerometer (poor MEMS part) during a GPS dropout / tunnel segment.
ev: ekf_orchestrator.dart:713 requires accelVar<0.5 AND gyroVar<0.1 to collect bias; ZUPT check at 357-359 needs accelVar<0.1 and gyroVar<0.01. A noisy accel keeps variance above these, so _biasInitialized stays false (line 720-731) and DR keeps raw bias. sensor_fusion.dart:204-213 also integrates raw event.x/y with only a fixed 0.9 decay, no noise model.
fix: Static-bias estimation and ZUPT never trigger because their variance thresholds are never met, so accelerometer bias is never removed and the 1-D position integrates unbounded drift; station snaps get rejected by the σ gate — DR position is meaningless, alarm fires late or not at all.

desc: Low max sensor sample rate or aggressive sensor batching (power-saving SoCs deliver IMU samples in bursts, not at ~100Hz).
ev: ekf_orchestrator.dart:69,87-88 hardcode window sizes as '~1s at 100Hz'; sensor_fusion.dart:189 computes dt from DateTime.now() (wall clock, ≈0 in a batch drain) and uses it for _velX/_velY integration (204-213). extractMotionFeatures (588) derives sampleRateHz from timestamps, which collapses under batching. No de-batching or per-sample event-timestamp handling.
fix: EKF windows assume ~100Hz; batched samples are processed in a tight loop where DateTime.now() dt≈0, corrupting velocity integration, the feature-extractor's computed sampleRateHz, and time-based ZUPT/motion gating — motion misclassification and bad DR during the exact dropout the EKF exists to cover.

desc: BRANCHING line splits: after a shared trunk the line forks (e.g. Y-branch); the rider's train takes the branch OPPOSITE to the prefetched one.
ev: trackingservice.dart:1143 metro deviation skipped; snap_to_route.dart windowed/heading logic only affects GPS snapping which isn't used for metro-leg progress; no branch/consist awareness in transfer_utils.extractTransitLegStops.
fix: After the divergence point the train is physically off-route, but metro-leg deviation is disabled so it's undetected; EKF continues integrating along the prefetched branch and fires the destination alarm at the modeled arc-length while the train is kilometres away on the other branch. Rider woken at wrong time and is on the wrong branch with no correct alarm.

desc: STALE prefetched station data: a newly-opened station exists on the line but is absent from the bundled static OSM asset (or a station is closed/renamed vs the asset).
ev: transfer_utils.dart:1155-1163 ('Completely ignores Google API num_stops. Uses ONLY OSM stops...') and :1368 (`numStops: actualNumStops` from OSM); all_india_stops.dart is a GENERATED static file with no runtime freshness check; _isActiveStop (transfer_utils.dart:236-249) only filters by a static status field.
fix: OSM asset is treated as the SOLE source of truth and Google's num_stops is explicitly ignored. A missing new station makes the modeled intermediate-stop count too low, so 'N stops before' is spaced too far apart and fires too LATE (rider can miss). A stale closed station still in the asset makes it fire too early (annoyance). Renamed stations give wrong labels. No versioning/expiry on the asset.

desc: SERVICE ENDS / last train DIVERTS TO DEPOT before reaching the rider's stop.
ev: trackingservice.dart:1143 metro deviation skipped; reroute_policy.dart onSustainedDeviation returns early when `!_online`; no early-termination / short-turn detection in trackingservice.dart.
fix: The train leaves the modeled route toward a depot. On the metro leg this divergence is invisible (deviation disabled), and EKF either keeps integrating and fires the destination alarm at the modeled arc-length (rider woken but train is heading to depot, not their stop) or the train terminates early and the rider must alight at an earlier station where progress is still below the alarm threshold, so NO alarm fires. Reroute cannot help underground/offline.

desc: SHORT-TURN: the boarded train terminates at an intermediate station short of the rider's destination (peak-hour short-turn working).
ev: Alarm firing requires progressMeters to reach the modeled threshold (alarm_evaluator.dart:796-797, 776-782); nothing detects that forward motion has permanently stopped short of the target; metro-leg deviation disabled (trackingservice.dart:1143).
fix: Train reaches an intermediate terminus and empties; EKF ZUPTs and stalls at that station's arc-length, which is below the destination/N-stops threshold, so the alarm never fires. The rider (asleep) is not warned to alight and does not learn they must change to a through train.

desc: Rider's phone is at low battery (forgot the powerbank) and the metro enters a long tunnel where GPS drops out — exactly the dead-reckoning scenario the EKF exists for.
ev: lib/config/power_policy.dart:49-57 (low tier: accuracy low, 50m filter, 40s dropout buffer). lib/services/tracking/location_stream_handler.dart:200 `_fftEnabled = batteryLevel >= 20;` disables FFT precisely when battery is low. EKF is only validated against one Bangalore ride (per task), so degraded-mode accuracy is unproven. Power tier keys off battery LEVEL only, not charging state, so a powerbank helps only by raising the level.
fix: PowerPolicy for <20% battery drops GPS to LocationAccuracy.low, distanceFilter 50m, and stretches gpsDropoutBuffer to 40s before fusion even engages; separately FFT (used for EKF station detection) is disabled below 20%. Degraded EKF progress in the tunnel underestimates position, so the 'N stops before' / distance alarm fires late or after the target stop.

desc: Rider props the phone flat on the tray table / seat and the train runs through a smooth-track tunnel (or briefly holds in the tunnel) with GPS unavailable.
ev: lib/core/ekf/zupt_detector.dart:58-75 degradedUltraQuietPath fires on accelVar<0.15 & gyroVar<0.05 & motionHint stationary independent of true velocity. Metro alarm progress can come from EKF s: lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1175-1185 (useEkfForAlarmProgress for metro/degraded). Thresholds are tuned to one ride's IMU (zupt_detector.dart:7-11 comments), so real-world quiet tunnels risk false ZUPT.
fix: In degraded mode EKF velocity drifts; if the phone is very still and the ride is smooth, the ZUPT detector's ultra-quiet path can falsely confirm a zero-velocity 'stop', pinning progress and under-counting distance/stops. The metro alarm (geometric progress) then fires late or never for that leg.

desc: Rider wears Bluetooth (or wired) earphones to sleep, alarm audio is captured by the headset, then they roll over / the buds fall out into a bag or dangle off the ear.
ev: lib/services/alarm_player.dart:13-24 sets AndroidUsageType.alarm (which many OEMs route to speaker, but not guaranteed) and iOS AVAudioSessionCategory.playback with mixWithOthers (follows active BT route). No becomingNoisy/route-change listener anywhere (grep found none). Vibration fallback: notification_service.dart:433-468 / alarm_haptics.dart.
fix: Alarm audio keeps playing into the disconnected/idle headset route and the rider hears little or nothing. There is no AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY handling and no forcing of the alarm to the loudspeaker; on iOS the AVAudioSession playback route follows the BT device. Only the vibration loop remains as a backstop.

desc: Rider opens the app to start a journey while already underground / inside a station with no GPS lock (cold start, no recent fix).
ev: _proceedWithDirections uses a cached position only if <30s old (homescreen.dart:511-530), else _getCurrentLocation()->Geolocator.getCurrentPosition() which returns null on failure (homescreen.dart:920-926). Null origin -> 'Could not get your current location' error dialog and tracking aborts (homescreen.dart:538-548). No last-known-position fallback (getLastKnownPosition is never called anywhere in lib/).
fix: getCurrentPosition throws underground, origin is null, so tracking never starts and the rider gets an error dialog instead of a monitored journey — or, if a stale cached fix exists, it starts but then gets no underground positions to evaluate.

desc: Train emerges from a long tunnel and the phone needs a fresh GNSS fix; with no mobile data there is no A-GPS assistance, so the first fix takes 20-60s+.
ev: Same root cause as the tunnel-blackout gap: alarm eval is position-driven (location_stream_handler.dart:268). Nothing bridges the post-tunnel fix latency — no time-based EKF alarm and no A-GPS/warm-start handling. gpsDropoutBuffer only triggers fusion start (location_stream_handler.dart:521-531), not alarm firing.
fix: During the cold-start window after surfacing, no positions arrive so the alarm still cannot evaluate; if the target stop sits at or just past the tunnel exit, the rider blows past it before the first fix lands.

desc: User granted 'Approximate location' only (Android 12+ coarse toggle), so the OS returns ~1-3km-accuracy fixes despite the app requesting high accuracy.
ev: PermissionService checks Permission.location.isGranted (permission_service.dart:31-51), which is TRUE for coarse-only grants; there is no ACCESS_FINE vs COARSE verification and no accuracy floor. LocationManager requests LocationAccuracy.high (location_manager.dart:45-48) but cannot force fine. Distance-mode fires on raw Geolocator.distanceBetween with no accuracy gate (alarm_controller.dart:425-460). GpsHealthMonitor's 50m poorAccuracy threshold (gps_health_monitor.dart:25) is never wired into production (only referenced by its own file + test).
fix: Distance/stop alarms compute against a fix that can be 1-3km off, firing kilometres early or, worse, reporting the rider as not-yet-near so the alarm fires late or never at the real stop.

desc: Rider (or Android auto-reset) has device master Location Services toggled OFF at the OS level while app location permission is still granted, or toggles it off mid-journey.
ev: Geolocator.isLocationServiceEnabled() / openLocationSettings() are never called anywhere in lib/ (grep returned nothing). Permission checks (permission_service.dart) verify grant status but not the service master switch. Mid-journey there is no detection: _checkGpsDropout only starts fusion (location_stream_handler.dart:521-531), which produces no alarm.
fix: At start, position acquisition fails (recoverable error dialog); mid-journey the position stream silently stops with no user-facing warning, so no alarm fires and the rider isn't told tracking is dead.

desc: Long one-stop intercity in distance mode where GPS drops to null for a stretch (tunnels/rural) while the train is geographically near the destination city but still far by rail (rail routes curve; straight-line << along-route distance).
ev: alarm_controller.dart:415-461: when progressMeters==null it computes Geolocator.distanceBetween(current,dest) vs alarmValue*1000 and fires; line 448 setDestinationAlarmFiredForKey(alarmKey,true) latches before triggering. EKF (route-aware DR) is not wired into this path, so there is no along-route fallback.
fix: Straight-line fallback fires the destination alarm hours early AND latches destinationAlarmFired=true, so the real arrival later is permanently suppressed -> rider is woken far too early, ignores it, then gets NO alarm at the actual stop.

desc: OS kills the foreground service mid-journey overnight (common on cheap India phones with aggressive OEM battery killers) and restarts it, but the route in the persisted snapshot has no usable 'directions' (minimization dropped it / large metro route) while the rider is in STOPS mode.
ev: trackingservice.dart:2049-2069 restores route only via restoreFromSnapshotIfDirectionsPresent; if absent, _evaluateGeofence (alarm_controller.dart:1233-1276) handles only alarmMode=='distance'/'time' — there is no stops branch. Snapshot directions are lossily minimized in tracking_state_store.dart:93-234.
fix: Route can't be restored, so stops evaluation is impossible; the geofence fallback only implements distance and time modes, so a stops/metro rider gets no further alarm and sleeps past the stop.

desc: OS kills the service in the first ~30s of a journey (before the first throttled snapshot write), e.g. rider starts tracking then pockets the phone and an OEM killer reaps it.
ev: location_stream_handler.dart:385-387 only saves a snapshot every >=30s; trackingservice.dart:2029-2089: on recovery with isActive but snapshot==null it logs 'No snapshot found, stopping self' and service.stopSelf().
fix: On restart the snapshot is null so the service calls stopSelf(); tracking silently dies for the entire journey with no alarm and no user indication.

desc: Very short non-metro journey in TIME mode that finishes in under ~30s or covers under 100m (short bus hop / last-mile), with 'wake me N min before'.
ev: location_stream_handler.dart:602-605 sets _timeAlarmEligible only when _distanceTravelledMeters>=100 && _etaSamples>=3 && sinceStart.inSeconds>=30; alarm_controller.dart:623-634 returns early (skips eval) for time mode when !timeAlarmEligible && !isMetroJourney.
fix: The time-alarm eligibility gate (>=100m traveled AND >=3 ETA samples AND >=30s since start) is never satisfied before arrival, so the time alarm is suppressed and never fires.

desc: App opened only seconds before departure with no time to prefetch; transit/stops journey where the directions API call is slow, times out, or fails on flaky station Wi-Fi/cell.
ev: homescreen.dart:592-619 builds directionsFuture and 'await directionsFuture'; stops validation and startTracking (homescreen.dart:803) run only after directions resolve; failures hit _showErrorDialog/return paths (e.g. homescreen.dart:877-884). Geofence fallback covers only distance/time (alarm_controller.dart:1250-1276).
fix: homescreen awaits the directions future and its validation before ever calling startTracking; on failure it shows an error and returns, so the rider who believes they armed the alarm actually has nothing running -> missed stop. No offline route means stops mode has no fallback.

desc: OS forces a reboot mid-journey (Android system update install, low-RAM kernel restart, scheduled restart on MIUI, or a battery-related shutdown on a cheap phone) while the rider is asleep on the train.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml has no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED and no <receiver>; MainActivity.kt contains only vibration + channel code (no boot handling); trackingservice.dart:212 autoStart:false; snapshot restore (snapshot_route_restorer.dart) is only wired to in-process resume, not boot.
fix: Tracking never comes back. There is no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and no BootReceiver in native code, and the background service is configured autoStart:false. After reboot the foreground service does not restart, the persisted TrackingSnapshot (saved every 30s in location_stream_handler.dart:381-414) is never used to resume tracking, and the rider gets no alarm.

desc: An incoming phone call arrives (or a call is already in progress) at the moment the wake-up alarm should fire — very likely for a rider whose family calls to check where they are.
ev: alarm_player.dart:13-24 (gainTransient focus, iOS mixWithOthers); no telephony/PhoneStateListener anywhere in lib (grep for phone/call/telephony found none). Native vibration uses USAGE_ALARM (MainActivity.kt startAlarmVibration) so vibration may still fire, but only if the UI isolate is alive to call the method channel.
fix: The alarm may be inaudible or ducked. AlarmPlayer requests only AndroidAudioFocus.gainTransient (lib/services/alarm_player.dart:17) rather than a stronger exclusive/alarm focus, and there is no phone-state (telephony) listener to detect the call, defer, or force the alarm onto the in-call/earpiece route. On iOS the session uses category playback + mixWithOthers (alarm_player.dart:20-23), which during a call typically yields to telephony. No fallback re-alerts after the call ends.

desc: Location permission is downgraded mid-journey (Android 'one-time'/'while in use' expiry, user toggles it, or the OS revokes background-location after inactivity) or the user toggles GPS/Location services off then on.
ev: location_manager.dart:86-101 (single subscription, onError logs only, no retry); no listener for permission changes or Geolocator.getServiceStatusStream in lib.
fix: GPS goes permanently silent for the rest of the trip. LocationManager subscribes to Geolocator.getPositionStream once and its onError callback only logs ('Real GPS Stream Error') with no re-subscription or recovery (lib/services/location_manager.dart:92-101). When Geolocator closes the stream on a permission/service error it is never re-established, so no further positions arrive, no alarm check runs, and (per the tunnel gap) the frozen EKF cannot substitute.

desc: User (or an OEM 'clean memory' one-tap button they habitually press before sleeping) force-stops the app from the task manager / app-info.
ev: trackingservice.dart:206-224 (autoStart:false, no restart-on-kill); no android:stopWithTask handling / restart service; detached lifecycle is acknowledged as unreliable in trackingservice.dart:506-513.
fix: Force-stop tears down every isolate and the foreground service; with no boot/restart receiver and autoStart:false, nothing revives tracking. Unlike a crash, force-stop also blocks alarms/receivers until the app is manually reopened. Rider gets no alarm and no indication tracking died.

desc: Android 13+ notification permission is revoked mid-journey (user swipes into settings, or the OS auto-revokes for an app they haven't opened in a while).
ev: notification_service.dart:724-741 relies on fullScreenIntent:true (needs notification permission); main.dart:78-83 checks permission only at launch; permission_service.dart:74-90 has no mid-journey re-validation; sound path (notification_service.dart:794-802) is independent of notification posting.
fix: The full-screen intent wake-up notification cannot be posted, so the lockscreen visual + insistent notification alerting is lost, and on newer Android the foreground-service notification suppression can cause the OS to stop the service. The app never re-checks or re-requests notification permission after startup (only checked once in main.dart:78-83 and permission_service.dart:74-90). Alarm audio via AlarmPlayer may still play IF the UI isolate is alive, so it degrades rather than fully fails.

desc: iOS rider (product is Flutter Android+iOS): screen locks and the app is backgrounded during the ride.
ev: ios/Runner/Info.plist:1-58 (no UIBackgroundModes present; grep returned none); trackingservice.dart:219-223 iOS config; alarm delivery depends on an alive isolate which iOS suspends.
fix: Background location and background audio are not declared. ios/Runner/Info.plist has the NSLocation usage strings but NO UIBackgroundModes key (no 'location'/'audio' entries), and IosConfiguration relies on onForeground/onBackground (trackingservice.dart:219-223). Without UIBackgroundModes, iOS suspends the app on lock, GPS stops, and the alarm cannot fire — total product death on iOS.

desc: NEW DIMENSION accessibility — deaf / hard-of-hearing, low-vision, elderly and cognitively-impaired riders, and screen-reader users. The wake cue assumes an audio-first rider with vibration and a visual takeover as backups; none of these degrade gracefully for disabled riders. A Deaf rider relies solely on vibration, which is useless if the phone rests on a soft seat/lap rather than in contact with the body, and there is only one fixed vibration pattern with no wearable/flash escalation. Low-vision riders get a visual full-screen alarm with no guaranteed large-text/high-contrast/TTS spoken-stop cue. The arming UI (station autocomplete, alarm-mode config) is never validated for TalkBack/VoiceOver.
ev: Single fixed vibration constant (notification_service.dart:408-416); no camera-flash/torch alert, no wearable-companion, no repeated-escalating haptic. Alarm audio is not accompanied by a spoken 'your stop is next' TTS. No semantics/accessibility labels evidence in homescreen.dart search/alarm UI; no large-text or high-contrast alarm-screen mode. Accessibility is entirely absent from all 6 existing dimensions.
fix: A Deaf rider whose phone is not against their body feels nothing and sleeps past the stop (product death for that population). Low-vision or elderly riders cannot reliably arm the alarm or perceive the wake cue. Zero accessibility consideration in a mass-market India-first app excludes and endangers a large user segment.

desc: NEW DIMENSION first-run / onboarding / permission-education failure. There is no onboarding flow at all, yet correct operation depends on the rider manually doing things the OS will not prompt for: whitelisting the app from battery optimization (no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS prompt exists), granting 'Allow all the time' background location (which on Android 11+ cannot be granted inline and needs a Settings trip), granting exact-alarm/full-screen-intent special access on Android 14+, and enabling POST_NOTIFICATIONS. If any is missed or denied on the very first journey, tracking silently under-performs or dies with no guided remediation.
ev: No onboarding/intro/tutorial/welcome files exist in lib (find returned nothing). Notification permission is requested but denial is not handled to explain consequences (main.dart:79-81, permission_service.dart:77-88). No isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations / battery-optimization whitelist prompt anywhere (consistent with the existing device-hardware CRITICAL). locationAlways cannot be granted inline (permission_service.dart:70) and there is no in-app deep-link/education to fix it.
fix: A first-time rider arms an alarm believing it will work, but background location is only 'while in use', battery optimization is on, or notifications are denied — so the first real overnight journey silently fails. No onboarding teaches the OEM-specific whitelisting that Indian budget phones require, and denial paths dead-end instead of guiding the user to Settings.

desc: NEW DIMENSION legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mistimed wake. A missed stop is not just 'product death' commercially — it can strand a sleeping rider alone at a terminus, a depot siding, or an unfamiliar unsafe area late at night (India-first, overnight sleeper use case). There is no liability disclaimer, no 'do not rely on this as your only alarm' messaging, no safety framing for the woken-but-disoriented rider, and (per route-topology gaps) the app can actively wake the rider at the WRONG place with false confidence.
ev: No terms/disclaimer or 'secondary alarm recommended' copy in the app. The wrong-direction / wrong-train / branch / depot-diversion route-topology cases already fire a confidently-wrong alarm (metro legs ignore deviation, trackingservice.dart:1120-1143). No safety-net messaging on the alarm screen, no 'you may be at the wrong stop' hedge.
fix: A rider harmed by a silent miss (stranded, safety incident) plus a product that made an implicit reliability promise creates real liability exposure; conversely a spuriously-confident wrong-place alarm (wrong-train/branch/depot cases) actively directs a groggy rider to alight in the wrong location. Neither the legal disclaimer nor the human-safety dimension is considered anywhere.

desc: NEW DIMENSION internationalization of station/place names (multilingual India: Kannada, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Urdu/RTL). The station corpus and matching are English-only, so a rider who reads/searches in a local script cannot find their station, and — more dangerously — the OSM-vs-Google station-name matching that drives stop-counting can silently fail across script/transliteration variants (e.g. 'Majestic' vs 'ಮೆಜೆಸ್ಟಿಕ್', 'Baiyappanahalli' spelling variants), dropping or mislabeling stops and corrupting 'N stops before'.
ev: all_india_stops.dart contains only ASCII/English names (non-ASCII grep returned nothing). No app localization: no localizationsDelegates/supportedLocales/AppLocalizations usage in lib (grep empty). Stop modeling relies on string-based OSM name matching (transfer_utils.dart), which is brittle across scripts/transliterations. This compounds the existing route-topology 'stale/renamed station' GAP.
fix: Non-English-literate riders can't reliably arm a journey; and transliteration mismatches between Google's returned names and the static OSM asset cause stops to be unmatched/miscounted, so 'N stops before' is spaced wrong and fires late — a miss, not just a cosmetic issue. No TTS/pronunciation of the target stop in the rider's language either.

desc: Android 14+ rider (increasingly common on newer budget phones) installs fresh. The wake alarm relies on a full-screen intent to light up the lockscreen. On Android 14+, USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is granted by default only to apps in the alarm/calling category; a generic app must be granted 'full-screen notifications' special access.
ev: Manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and notification_service.dart:729 sets fullScreenIntent:true ('critical for lockscreen appearance'), but grep for canUseFullScreenIntent|requestFullScreenIntentPermission returns nothing. No code queries or requests the Android 14+ special access.
fix: The full-screen alarm UI is demoted to a normal notification behind the lockscreen. On a silenced/dozing phone the rider is not forcefully woken; the alarm effectively under-fires. There is no runtime check nor education to request this special access.

desc: Cold first launch: main.dart fires _checkNotificationPermission() from initState, showing the bare Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS system prompt before the user has seen any explanation of what the app does. Reflexively the user taps 'Deny'.
ev: lib/main.dart:78-83 _checkNotificationPermission() calls Permission.notification.request() with no rationale/priming, at app-launch, before onboarding. PermissionService._requestNotificationPermission (permission_service.dart) does handle the permanent-denial case with _showSettingsDialog, so it is not a total GAP — but the un-primed early prompt makes permanent denial likely.
fix: POST_NOTIFICATIONS becomes denied (and after a second denial, permanently denied). Since the wake-up is delivered via a notification channel, a permanent denial later dead-ends: the only remedy PermissionService offers is a Settings dialog the sleepy rider must navigate. Poor priming turns a recoverable prompt into a permanent block.

desc: At the 'Wake Me' rationale/background dialog the (hurried, already-boarding) rider taps 'Not Now' or 'Cancel' instead of Continue.
ev: permission_service.dart _showRationaleDialog returns false on 'Not Now'; the caller returns false. homescreen.dart _onWakeMePressed else branch only does setState(() => _isLoading = false) — no _showErrorDialog, relying on the incorrect assumption that 'the service already showed the user a dialog'. When the rider declined the rationale, no dialog was shown afterward.
fix: The flow returns false with no follow-up. The user presses Wake Me, dismisses the dialog, and the button silently resets to idle with nothing happening and no error toast — the rider reasonably assumes the alarm is armed when it is not.

desc: Rider grants everything correctly on the very first journey, but there is no post-setup confirmation that tracking will actually survive a locked, dozing screen (no readiness check combining background-location + battery-whitelist + notification + full-screen-intent status).
ev: No aggregated readiness/health screen exists; grep for onboard|tutorial|firstRun|hasSeen returns nothing and SplashScreen (splash_screen.dart) only restores session state. PermissionService returns a single bool with no per-condition surfacing of battery-optimization or full-screen-intent status (neither of which it even checks).
fix: The rider gets no signal distinguishing 'armed and will really work' from 'armed but will silently die', so the first real overnight trip is the test — and if any OEM/battery condition is off, they discover it by missing the stop.

desc: The heartbeat 'foreground process was killed' safety net is expected to detect loss of tracking on iOS the way it does for Android app-swipe.
ev: heartbeat_monitor.dart runs on Timer.periodic inside the background isolate (isEnabled gated on _isBackgroundIsolate, trackingservice.dart:625-627) which iOS pauses; its timeout handler calls NotificationService().showTrackingPaused() (heartbeat_monitor.dart) via show(), unavailable while suspended. The whole design comment says it detects the foreground being 'swiped away/killed' — an Android model that doesn't map to iOS suspension.
fix: On iOS the foreground and the background isolate are suspended together, so the heartbeat monitor cannot detect anything (it too is frozen), and even if it did, its recovery action is another show() notification that cannot be delivered while suspended. The one watchdog is inoperative on iOS.

desc: iOS rider on a cheap/older phone in Low Power Mode (common in India-first market, and common for someone who dozed off with a low battery) backgrounds the app.
ev: No significant-location-change / CLVisit / BGTaskScheduler usage anywhere (grep of location_stream_handler.dart and lib/ finds none). The service is configured autoStart:false (trackingservice.dart:220) and start-on-demand only, so once suspended nothing re-launches it.
fix: Low Power Mode makes iOS even more aggressive about suspending and denying background execution and location. With no significant-location-change or CLVisit monitoring registered as a coarse fallback, there is literally no code path that can wake the app to re-evaluate the alarm.

desc: Storage-full device: snapshot persistence fails (SharedPreferences refuses the write or the directions payload is too large), then the isolate is later killed and the OS happens to restart it.
ev: saveSnapshot (tracking_state_store.dart:339-390) logs 'SharedPreferences refused snapshot write' and rethrows on payload-too-large; loadSnapshot (tracking_state_store.dart:391-403) returns null on missing/corrupt data, and the recovery branch (trackingservice.dart:2029-2030) simply does nothing when snapshot==null. No ETA-time OS alarm exists to backstop the lost snapshot.
fix: Recovery loads a null/stale snapshot and cannot restore the route, so tracking is silently dead even though a restart occurred — and there is still no scheduled fallback alarm to cover the gap.

desc: An uncaught exception in the background isolate (EKF pipeline, reroute decision, or ETA math throws on unexpected real-world input) crashes the isolate mid-ride.
ev: _onStart wires reroute handling that awaits _handleRerouteDecision (trackingservice.dart:1806-1810) and other listeners without an isolate-level supervisor; there is no external process/AlarmManager job monitoring liveness. The only monitor (heartbeat_monitor.dart) shares the isolate's fate, and no independent scheduled notification exists as a last resort.
fix: The isolate terminates; because the watchdog (HeartbeatMonitor) is itself inside that isolate, nothing external observes the death and no alarm fires.

desc: A hard-of-hearing rider wears Bluetooth hearing aids / BT earbuds and relies on them to hear anything. They arm the alarm and doze; audio is their primary channel.
ev: lib/services/alarm_player.dart _alarmAudioContext hardcodes AudioContextAndroid(usageType: AndroidUsageType.alarm, audioFocus: gainTransient) and always setVolume(1.0); there is no companion-device / hearing-aid routing option and no user control over output route. The comment at lines 29-34 confirms the deliberate force-to-alarm-stream choice, made only for the media-volume-zero case, with no consideration of BT-routed hearing aids.
fix: AlarmPlayer forces the Android ALARM usage stream, which on most OEMs is pinned to the phone's built-in loudspeaker and is NOT routed to the paired hearing-aid/BT media sink. The rider's aids stay silent; with vibration also unreliable (see seat scenario) they perceive no cue.

desc: A low-vision rider has set the OS system font size to Large / 200% (extremely common on cheap India-first phones used by elderly). They open the home screen to arm the alarm.
ev: lib/screens/homescreen.dart sizes containers with SizedBox(height: screenHeight*0.3) for the map and fixed screenHeight/screenWidth fractions for padding, while text uses TextStyle(fontSize: screenWidth*0.045 / *0.05); maptracking.dart uses const TextStyle(fontSize:16/26). grep shows NO textScaler/textScaleFactor/MediaQuery override or clamp anywhere in lib/, so nothing guards against overflow at large scale and there is no large-text/simplified mode.
fix: The arming layout is built from fixed fractions of screen size while text scales with the OS setting, so labels, the 'Alert me N stops prior' box, the slider label, and the 'Wake Me!' button overflow/clip or collide; the rider cannot read the current threshold or reliably arm the alarm.

desc: A blind TalkBack (or VoiceOver) user swipes through the home screen to set how many stops before their destination to be woken.
ev: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1190-1245: GestureDetector(onTap: showDialog...) -> Container -> Text with no Semantics/button wrapper. grep -c Semantics on homescreen.dart returns 0; zero semanticLabel usage exists in all of lib/.
fix: The stop/distance/time threshold control is a bare GestureDetector wrapping a Container+Text, so the screen reader announces only the static text 'Alert me 2 stops prior' with no button role and no hint it is actionable. The user cannot discover that tapping opens the value dialog, and cannot change the threshold — they either accept a wrong default or abandon arming.

desc: A blind rider needs to know WHICH stop to get off at when woken (they cannot glance at the map). The alarm fires in a tunnel near the target station.
ev: lib/services/notification_service.dart showWakeUpAlarm takes only title/body strings; ensureAlarmNotificationVisible defaults to 'Time to Wake Up!'/'Approaching destination' (lines 858-860). No flutter_tts/TextToSpeech dependency exists (absent from pubspec.yaml and grep of lib/); the full-screen takeover in maptracking.dart is plain Text with no spoken equivalent.
fix: The wake cue carries no spoken stop-name. The notification title/body are generic ('Time to Wake Up!' / 'Approaching destination') and there is no TTS announcement of the actual station, so even a rider who hears the alarm has no accessible way to learn which stop is next or confirm it's theirs — they may exit at the wrong station or panic.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: The app makes an implicit 'we will wake you' reliability promise with zero legal or safety caveat anywhere. A rider treats WakePoint as their sole alarm for an overnight/late-night ride, it fails (any cause below), and they are stranded — then look for who is responsible.
ev: Full grep of lib/ for disclaimer|liabilit|not rely|backup alarm|do not rely|terms of|consent returns ZERO user-facing hits (only a code comment in lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:47 'It does not rely on events lists' and reliability comments about notifications). User-facing copy is purely confident: 'Time to Wake Up!' (lib/services/notification_service.dart:858), 'Arriving at Destination' (lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:90,112). Permission rationale even over-promises: 'we need to send you a notification to wake you up!' (lib/services/permission_service.dart:83).
fix: No disclaimer, no Terms of Service/consent, no 'do not rely on this as your only alarm', no reliability caveat, and no in-app safety framing exist. A harmed rider (stranded alone at a terminus late at night, safety incident) has an unqualified reliability promise to point at, creating direct liability exposure; nothing ever told them to set a backup.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Degraded route context: route metadata/transitLegs is empty or lost (cold restart mid-journey, cache miss, or a fixture-like partial route), while the rider is somewhere along the corridor.
ev: lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:73-118 — when transitLegs.isEmpty it fires eventType finalDestination message 'Arriving at Destination' via 'Direct Fire: destination < 200m' (line 86-92) or 'Destination (60% remaining rule)' at progressMeters >= start + 40% (line 106-114), with no branch/parallel-track verification and identical copy to the validated path.
fix: The evaluator's fallback path fires a confident 'Arriving at Destination' alarm on a bare geometric rule (<200m OR 40% into the final leg) with no leg/topology validation. A groggy rider is actively directed to alight, potentially at the wrong place, with the same authoritative wording used for a genuine, validated arrival — a spuriously-confident wrong-place wake.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Groggy rider is woken by the alarm one or two stops early, silences the looping sound, and falls back asleep before their actual stop.
ev: lib/services/alarm_evaluator.dart:159-168 — RULE 1 returns null once firedLegIds contains the leg id ('Leg already fired, skipping'). No snooze/re-arm/escalation logic exists (grep for snooze|rearm|re-arm in trackingservice/alarm_evaluator finds none). Alarm persistence is only ongoing:true/loop for the FIRST firing (notification_service.dart:733-734), not a re-trigger after user dismissal.
fix: The strict one-alarm-per-leg rule marks the leg fired and suppresses every subsequent evaluation for that leg, so there is NO second/escalating wake before the stop and no snooze-then-re-alarm. A single missed acknowledgment converts into a full missed stop — a very common failure mode for a genuinely sleepy user, with no safety re-arm.

area: iOS RELIABILITY — the honest ceiling for a 2h scre
desc: iOS background operation is completely non-functional today, and the app's core mechanic (IMU/EKF dead-reckoning through a tunnel) is structurally impossible on iOS in the way it is on Android. Concretely: (1) ios/Runner/Info.plist has NO UIBackgroundModes key at all — the instant the screen locks, iOS suspends the app and Geolocator delivers nothing (HARD FACT, confirmed by reading Info.plist lines 4-60). (2) All three location call-sites (lib/screens/maptracking.dart:616, lib/services/position/gps_position_provider.dart:28, lib/services/location_manager.dart:45) use plain `LocationSettings`, never geolocator's `AppleSettings`, so even with the background mode added, `allowBackgroundLocationUpdates` defaults to false and background delivery never turns on (HARD FACT). (3) The deeper, un-closable problem: CoreMotion (accelerometer/gyro that feeds sensors_plus and the EKF) does NOT run while the app is suspended — iOS grants no background mode for raw IMU. The location background mode keeps the app RUNNING (not merely un-terminated) only while location events keep arriving; in a deep metro tunnel with no GPS and no cell/wifi fix, updates stop, iOS suspends the process, CoreMotion stops, and the EKF freezes. So the exact scenario WakePoint exists to solve — dead-reckon through a tunnel — cannot execute on iOS by continuous-tracking means alone. AppDelegate.swift is bare (no AVAudioSession, no AlarmKit bridge), and alarm_controller.dart's one-shot latch has no iOS system-alarm path, so a suspended app has no way to make noise.
ev: Un-closable / honest gaps on iOS even after all fixes: (1) TRUE deep-tunnel dead-reckoning is impossible. Once iOS suspends the app (no GPS + no cell in a long tunnel), CoreMotion stops and the EKF freezes — iOS grants no background mode for raw IMU. The system does not deliver a suspension warning, so the app cannot 'coast' on IMU the way Android (with a wakelock/foreground service) can. WakePoint's headline capability is therefore degraded to 'best available ETA snapshot taken at tunnel entry, fired as a fixed-time system alarm' rather than live inertial tracking. (2) This makes wake accuracy dependent on ETA-prediction quality: if the train runs faster than the pre-tunnel estimate, a conservative (early) fixed alarm still wakes the rider in time, but a mis-scheduled alarm could fire late = product death. Mitigation is scheduling early + the geofence backstop, but there is irreducible risk on long final tunnel segments with variable speed. (3) AlarmKit requires iOS 26+ (shipped late 2025). India's iOS base skews to older/cheaper devices, so a meaningful slice falls to the weaker Time-Sensitive-notification fallback, which a user can theoretically dismiss/disable and which does not bypass the ring switch on its own. (4) The Critical Alerts entitlement is realistically a denial for an indie transit alarm (hand-vetted, life-safety-only) — do not design around it. (5) If Apple's reviewer disputes the persistent-location justification under Guideline 2.5.4, background location can be rejected; the AlarmKit + geofence path partially survives that but with degraded ETA refinement. (6) Silent-audio keep-alive would technically hold the app (and CoreMotion) alive through a tunnel, but it is an active Guideline 2.5.4 rejection risk and is deliberately excluded. NET: iOS cannot match Android's reliability for the tunnel dead-reckoning case; AlarmKit rescues the wake guarantee for iOS 26+ users but shifts it from spatial-live to temporal-scheduled. Recommend iOS as fast-follow behind an Android-first launch.
fix: 1. Info.plist (ios/Runner/Info.plist, after line 59): add <key>UIBackgroundModes</key><array><string>location</string></array>. Add <key>NSAlarmKitUsageDescription</key><string>WakePoint schedules an alarm to wake you before your stop even if the app is in the background.</string>. Keep NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription (already present line 52). Do NOT add the 'audio' background mode unless/until a silent-audio keep-alive is deliberately chosen (Guideline 2.5.4 risk).; 2. Turn on real background location: in lib/screens/maptracking.dart:616, lib/services/position/gps_position_provider.dart:28, and lib/services/location_manager.dart:45, replace the plain `LocationSettings(...)` with a platform-branched geolocator `AppleSettings(accuracy: LocationAccuracy.high, activityType: ActivityType.automotiveNavigation, distanceFilter: 0, pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically: false, showBackgroundLocationIndicator: true, allowBackgroundLocationUpdates: true)`. Centralize this in one factory so all three sites share it.

desc: iOS notification permission is never requested through the permission flow — permission_service short-circuits notifications on non-Android.
ev: permission_service.dart L74-75: _requestNotificationPermission returns true immediately when !Platform.isAndroid, so no iOS UNUserNotification authorization is requested here (it depends on whatever flutter_local_notifications does at init, which is not guaranteed).
fix: Explicitly request iOS notification authorization (alert/sound/badge, and critical-alert entitlement if the alarm must override silent/DND) via flutter_local_notifications' iOS init or Permission.notification on iOS.

desc: Persistent cache is TTL-evicted after 5 min even for offline restore, undermining 'cached route = offline ground truth'. RouteCache.get applies defaultTtl=5min AND deletes the entry on expiry (route_cache.dart:130-134); OfflineCoordinator.getRoute offline path calls _cache.get with that default TTL (offline_coordinator.dart:166-171). So a route cached >5 min ago is unavailable/destroyed when offline, throwing 'Offline and no cached route available' (offline_coordinator.dart:173). Mid-session this is masked because geometry is held in memory, but any offline cold-restart (app killed by Xiaomi/Samsung memory manager, then no signal in a tunnel) loses the route entirely.
ev: route_cache.dart:130-134 (TTL check deletes key), offline_coordinator.dart:166-173 (offline get uses default TTL then throws).
fix: Pass a much longer (or infinite) TTL on the offline read path, and never delete the entry during an offline get -- distinguish 'stale for cost' from 'usable for offline continuity'.

desc: Server directions proxy performs zero route validation and caches errors/degenerate responses opportunistically. mapsController.googleApiProxy caches any 2xx body (mapsController.js:24-27) and forwards Google status verbatim; the client only checks status==OK and routes non-empty (direction_service.dart:206-209). ZERO_RESULTS or a metro-less driving fallback is accepted as-is. Combined with the 09:00 anchor fallback, a rider can be tracked against a route that does not actually reflect current service.
ev: mapsController.js:9-36 (generic proxy, caches response.data unconditionally on 2xx), direction_service.dart:206-270 (accepts first route, promotes fastest metro-containing route but falls back to 'fastest available route' with no metro leg at 253-259).
fix: Validate on the server or client that a transit request actually returned a transit route before caching/using it; refuse to silently downgrade a metro journey to a walking/driving polyline.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: Only TIME mode has a minimum-eligibility gate; STOPS and DISTANCE modes can fire on the very first tick, and DISTANCE falls back to straight-line GPS distance which mismeasures winding routes.
ev: Time gate at location_stream_handler.dart:602-604 and alarm_controller.dart:623-634; metro bypasses it (:626). No equivalent gate before the stops geometric check or the distance checks (alarm_controller.dart:412-540, 722-806). Straight-line fallback uses Geolocator.distanceBetween(user,dest) (:425-431, :811-818) instead of remaining route distance.
fix: Add a small warm-up/eligibility gate (samples + moved distance) to stops/distance modes; prefer route-arc remaining distance over crow-flies, using straight-line only as a last resort with an inflation factor.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: Product spec references 4 alarm modes (stops-before, minutes-before, distance-before, time-before) but the code implements only 3 (stops, time, distance); 'time-before' and 'minutes-before' are the same AlarmMode.time path.
ev: enum AlarmMode { stops, time, distance } (alarm_evaluator.dart:6); mode mapping in alarm_controller.dart:613-618 collapses anything non-stops/non-time to distance.
fix: Confirm intended mode set; if a distinct clock-time ('wake me by 07:45') mode is required it does not exist and must be added — today it silently maps to distance.

desc: On UI death the app flips to a 'paused' state and replaces the journey notification with a 'Tracking paused' one (D3 partially confirmed). This is misleading for a sleeping rider who deliberately swiped the app away, and it advertises a degraded state even though GPS/alarm evaluation actually keep running.
ev: heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-98: after a 4 s heartbeat gap it calls TrackingStateStore.setPaused(true), cancelJourneyProgress(), showTrackingPaused(), then stop()s itself. It does NOT stop the location stream or alarm evaluation (checkAndTriggerAlarm in alarm_controller.dart:298-330 is gated only by trackingSessionActive, never by isPaused). notification_service.dart:497 and :995 suppress journey-progress updates while paused. So the claim 'pauses/stops tracking' is only half true: tracking continues, but the UX declares it paused and the progress notification disappears.
fix: Do not treat UI-swipe as a pause. Keep the journey progress notification alive from the background isolate and drop the 'Tracking paused' notification for the swipe-away case (reserve it for genuine location/permission loss). Ensure the paused flag never gates alarm delivery.

desc: foregroundServiceType 'mediaPlayback' is declared as a workaround to keep audio alive, but on Android 14+ starting an FGS of type mediaPlayback without an active MediaSession can be rejected, and 'location' type requires background-location to already be granted at start. If either FGS-type start is refused the service won't come up.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml:52-54 declares foregroundServiceType="location|mediaPlayback"; the matching runtime perms exist (lines 9-10). But there is no MediaSession anywhere in the codebase, and background-location is only requested via a rationale flow that the user can decline (permission_service.dart:59-72) while tracking can still be attempted. Android 14 throws on FGS start if the declared type's preconditions aren't met.
fix: Verify ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is granted before startService; drop mediaPlayback from the FGS type (or back it with a real MediaSession) and instead keep alarm audio alive via a wake lock + USAGE_ALARM playback, which does not require the mediaPlayback FGS type.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: Do-Not-Disturb 'Total Silence' is not handled. Alarm-usage audio (AndroidUsageType.alarm) survives ringer-silent/vibrate, but a user with a full DND rule that also silences alarms will get no sound; the app never requests notification-policy access nor marks the channel to bypass DND.
ev: alarm_player.dart:13-24 uses USAGE_ALARM (good for ringer-silent). grep for ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY|NotificationPolicy|bypassDnd|setBypassDnd returns nothing; the alarm channel (notification_service.dart:610-619 / MainActivity.kt) is not set to bypass DND.
fix: Request ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY and set the alarm channel to bypass DND (setBypassDnd(true)) where the user grants it; surface a setup warning if DND is set to block alarms. This is India-first budget-relevant because many users keep phones on aggressive silence overnight.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: Single-shot notification with no delivery verification or re-arm on failure. showWakeUpAlarm wraps the show/play/vibrate in a try/catch that on ANY exception just logs and resets _alarmCurrentlyShowing=false — one failed post = permanently missed alarm (the destination latch may already be set), with no retry loop, no escalation, and no confirmation the sound is actually audible.
ev: notification_service.dart:783-835 (single Future.wait for sound+vibration+notification; catch at 827-835 just resets the guard). The destination fired-latch is set before/around the trigger (alarm_controller.dart:683,777,828,1207) so a swallowed failure is not retried at the delivery layer; only AlarmEvaluator-path notification exceptions roll back fired markers (alarm_controller.dart:1214-1225), not the distance/time/geofence direct paths.
fix: Add a delivery watchdog: after firing, verify AlarmPlayer.isPlaying and the notification is active; if not, retry with backoff and escalate (e.g. re-fire, or trigger the exact-alarm backstop). Don't set the fired-latch until delivery is confirmed.

desc: Rider is on low battery (or forces battery-saver on) expecting the app to conserve power without losing accuracy.
ev: PowerPolicyManager.forBatteryLevel (power_policy.dart:28-57) returns accuracy/distanceFilter tiers, but location_manager.dart:45-48 hardcodes LocationAccuracy.high, distanceFilter:0 and start() (line 94) always uses that. location_stream_handler.dart:194-200 and trackingservice.dart:2136-2141 only consume policy.gpsDropoutBuffer/notificationTick — never accuracy/distanceFilter.
fix: The low/medium PowerPolicy tiers (LocationAccuracy.low/medium, larger distanceFilter) are computed but never applied — GPS always runs at high accuracy/distanceFilter 0, draining the battery faster, so a low phone dies sooner mid-journey (see reboot GAP). The 'power saving' is dead code.

desc: New Android (API 34/35) where USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is restricted to calling/alarm-category apps — a general utility app's full-screen alarm may be downgraded to a normal notification.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and MainActivity showWhenLocked/turnScreenOn, targetSdkVersion 34 (android/app/build.gradle:21). No runtime canUseFullScreenIntent() check or fallback is present; on API34+ the intent is only auto-granted to eligible categories, otherwise it surfaces as a heads-up notification. (Audio via alarm_player may still ring, mitigating.)
fix: The wake-up screen may not turn on / show over the lockscreen; if the rider relies on the visual full-screen alarm they may sleep through it.

desc: Device clock jumps mid-journey (NTP correction, dual-SIM network time change, or user sets manual time) while tracking underground/near the stop.
ev: GPS dropout detection uses wall clock: location_stream_handler.dart:525 silentFor = DateTime.now().difference(last) vs gpsDropoutBuffer. sensor_fusion.dart:189 dt from DateTime.now(). Speed derivation is guarded (location_manager.dart:188,202-207 require dt>minDt and clamp), and the IMU EKF timestamp uses a monotonic Stopwatch (sensor_fusion.dart:178,226), which limits but does not fully prevent the dropout-detection error.
fix: A backward jump makes 'silentFor' negative so a real GPS dropout is not detected (fusion never engaged); a forward jump triggers a false dropout and spins up sensor fusion unnecessarily; IMU dt also corrupts one integration step.

desc: Storage full on a cheap 32GB phone so Hive writes fail when caching the prefetched route and persisting tracking snapshots.
ev: route_cache.dart:163-168 put() has no try/catch (caller in direction_service.dart:331 swallows it, so the live route survives). Snapshot save in location_stream_handler.dart:389-413 catches and only logs failure. Recovery at trackingservice.dart:2029-2090 calls stopSelf() when loadSnapshot() returns null. route_cache.dart:75-83 even deletes the box on open failure, discarding prior cache.
fix: Route-cache and snapshot writes throw; the current journey continues from in-memory data, but no snapshot is saved, so if the OS later kills the isolate the recovery flow finds no fresh snapshot and stops itself — silent loss of tracking after process death.

desc: Phone overheats in a hot bag/pocket (Indian summer, cheap phone) and the SoC thermally throttles the CPU during the ride.
ev: No thermal state monitoring anywhere. Alarm evaluation is only invoked from _handlePositionUpdate (location_stream_handler.dart:268-273) via onCheckAlarm; the periodic _handleGpsCheckTick (428-452) does NOT evaluate alarms, so if position processing is starved, no timer-based safety net fires the alarm.
fix: Heavy EKF/FFT compute and the alarm pipeline run slower on the background isolate; alarm evaluation (which only runs on position callbacks) can lag, and throttling can starve the isolate, delaying a stop alarm.

desc: EXPRESS / skip-stop train: rider sets "3 stops before" on a line where the boarded train runs express and skips the modeled intermediate stations (common on Indian suburban rail / some metro peak services).
ev: alarm_evaluator.dart:775-797 counts passed stops solely by distance (progressMeters>=sm), with no notion of whether the train physically stopped; transfer_utils.dart:1164-1368 models stops from the static OSM asset, not from the actual service pattern.
fix: Alarm still fires at the geographic position of the Nth-from-last MODELED stop (progressMeters>=stopMeters), but the express train makes 0-1 physical stops between the alarm point and the destination and travels faster, so the rider's real warning window collapses from an expected ~5 min to seconds; the '3 stops' shown is fictional. If the rider's own destination is a skipped minor stop, the train blows past it (routing failure) though the rider is at least woken.

desc: TRAIN SPLITS mid-route: a consist divides into two portions bound for different destinations and the rider is seated in the wrong half.
ev: No consist/portion model exists (route is a single polyline in RouteModel/route_models.dart); metro-leg progress is EKF arc-length (trackingservice.dart:1183-1185) with deviation disabled (trackingservice.dart:1143).
fix: App has no concept of train consist or which half the rider is in; after the split the rider's physical path diverges from the prefetched route. On a metro leg this is undetectable (deviation off, EKF marches along modeled route), so the destination alarm fires at the modeled distance regardless of which half the rider rode. Rider misses.

desc: SINGLE-STATION HOP: destination is only 1-2 stops away, so there is very little runway (short leg, possibly high speed).
ev: alarm_evaluator.dart:667-674 fires at metersInLeg>=legLength*0.4; alarm_controller.dart:277-286 delegates sound to foreground isolate ('audio playback ... may be delayed').
fix: With 0 modeled intermediate stops the alarm uses the 60%-distance rule (fire after 40% of the leg). On a 2-minute hop that is ~40-70s of warning at best; combined with background-isolate audio being delegated to the foreground isolate (added latency), a fast short hop can fire only seconds before arrival, effectively too late to gather belongings / stand up.

desc: REPLACEMENT BUS for a closed metro section: at planning time the section was open so the prefetched route is metro geometry, but the actual service is a road-following rail-replacement bus.
ev: isMetro is decided from cached directions vehicle type (transfer_utils.dart:251-275); metro legs skip soft-lock and use EKF (trackingservice.dart:1120-1143, 1175-1185); no runtime check that the metro section is actually operating.
fix: The leg is still flagged isMetro, so the app disables deviation checking and uses rail-tuned EKF dead-reckoning, while the bus follows a slower, geometrically different road path. Progress (EKF arc-length along metro geometry) desynchronizes badly from reality, producing a mistimed or spurious alarm. If instead Google had routed the bus as a non-metro leg, it would be handled — the gap is specifically stale metro data.

desc: LOOP / CIRCLE line where the route arc nearly closes on itself (chosen direction wraps most of the way around, so the polyline passes close to its own start).
ev: snap_to_route.dart:129-137 constrains search to a +/-25 segment window around the previous index, and :171 applies a +100 penalty for i<prevIdx-3 (hard resistance to backward movement) — both assume a simple non-self-approaching route.
fix: On elevated/GPS portions, snapping can mis-match between the near-touching outbound and return segments: the windowed search (+/-25 segments) plus the backward-movement penalty can either lock onto the wrong nearby segment or resist legitimate progress, causing progress jumps/stalls and thus a mistimed alarm. (Underground metro sections avoid this only because they bypass GPS snapping entirely and use EKF.)

desc: MISSED TRANSFER: rider must change lines mid-journey but oversleeps the transfer alarm (or the transfer walk) and stays on the first train past the interchange.
ev: transfer_utils.dart:382-715 builds transfer events and alarm_evaluator.dart:128-144 handles boundary overshoot for the previous metro leg; however leg advancement is purely geometric (alarm_controller.dart:897-919) and assumes the modeled transfer occurred; reroute is gated offline (reroute_policy.dart onSustainedDeviation `!_online`).
fix: Transfer detection itself is implemented and a transfer alarm fires N stops before the interchange, and boundary-overshoot handling still fires it if progress jumps past the exact switch point. But if the rider misses it and stays aboard, the app keeps evaluating the SECOND leg's stops (which assume the rider transferred), so subsequent alarms are anchored to the wrong physical line; there is no re-plan offline and no 'you failed to transfer' detection.

desc: Rider enables Do-Not-Disturb (or 'silent'/priority-only) before sleeping so notifications and calls won't wake them.
ev: Notification channel plays no sound (notification_service.dart:609-619 playSound:false) and alarm audio uses AudioAttributesUsage.alarm / category alarm (alarm_player.dart:13-24, notification_service.dart:731-732). This bypasses standard DND on Android but there is no runtime DND detection, no 'bypass DND' channel flag set, and no iOS critical-alert entitlement, so aggressive DND profiles remain a hole.
fix: If the sound were driven by the notification channel it would be suppressed under DND. The app instead plays via a dedicated alarm-usage audio stream, which Android normally exempts from DND — but custom 'Total silence' DND modes, or users who route alarms through DND, and iOS's notification-sound suppression can still mute the cue, leaving only vibration.

desc: A very deep sleeper needs a louder and longer alarm than a normal notification chime to actually wake.
ev: Looping is handled (alarm_player.dart:53 ReleaseMode.loop; INSISTENT+NO_CLEAR flags notification_service.dart:743). Volume is a single setVolume(1.0) capped by system alarm volume (alarm_player.dart:84-86) with no ramp/boost. Vibration pattern is a fixed constant (notification_service.dart:408-416) with no 'stronger' option.
fix: The alarm loops indefinitely (good for 'longer') but there is no gradually-escalating volume, no override of the system alarm volume to maximum, and a single fixed vibration pattern. A deep sleeper who left alarm volume low simply is not woken loudly enough.

desc: Rider stuffs the phone deep in a bag or trouser pocket to sleep, heavily attenuating GPS (accuracy balloons past 50m and fixes get intermittent).
ev: GpsHealthMonitor marks degraded at accuracy>50m (gps_health_monitor.dart:24-25,113). Soft-lock uses raw GPS accuracy and lateral offset on non-metro legs (trackingservice.dart:1143-1172). LocationManager treats sub-accuracy movement as jitter (location_manager.dart:196-207) which helps speed but not progress stalls. Fallback to EKF is exercised but validated on one ride only.
fix: Poor-accuracy fixes degrade snap-to-route progress; on a non-metro (bus/walk) leg the noisy lateral offset can trip the soft-lock/deviation logic and cause a spurious reroute, or simply stall progress so the distance/time alarm drifts. GPS health degrades to the EKF fallback which is under-validated.

desc: Rider dozes off holding the phone and it slips from the hand to the lap or floor, sharply re-orienting the device mid-journey.
ev: TiltFilter is a complementary gyro/accel filter that re-converges and gates on motion state (tilt_filter.dart:58-163, setMotionState). EKF is GPS-corrected when fixes arrive (sensor_fusion.dart:132-164 updateGps). The legacy raw-integration path in SensorFusionManager integrates device-frame accel with no gravity/tilt removal and resets every 10s (sensor_fusion.dart:186-220, 45-46) — but its fusedPositionStream is not what drives alarms, so impact is limited to the tunnel/no-GPS window.
fix: The sudden drop injects a large transient acceleration and a new device orientation. With GPS present the EKF re-anchors and the tilt filter re-converges, so progress is fine; but if the drop happens inside a tunnel (GPS gone) the transient can bias dead-reckoned velocity/position and shift the alarm timing.

desc: Rider switches on Airplane mode before sleeping (to save battery / block calls), assuming the prefetched route means everything still works offline.
ev: No airplane-mode or isLocationServiceEnabled handling found in tracking/permission code (grep returned nothing). Reroute requires fetching new directions over network (trackingservice.dart:1310-1320 _handleRerouteDecision). EKF/fusion require an initial GPS position to seed (sensor_fusion.dart:85-99, location_stream_handler.dart:541-574). Offline alarm eval itself works from cached route registry/events.
fix: If GNSS stays on and the route is already cached, GPS-driven alarms can still work; but airplane mode removes A-GPS (slow/cold first fix) and all networking, so no reroute is possible if the rider deviates, and on phones where airplane mode also disables location the EKF never gets an initial GPS anchor and progress/alarm never advance.

desc: On an Android 14+ budget phone, the phone is locked in the rider's pocket when the alarm should fire.
ev: Alarm relies on fullScreenIntent:true (notification_service.dart:729) and the manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml). There is no runtime check/request for the Android 14 special access (canUseFullScreenIntent) and no fallback strategy if it is denied; sound/vibration still play via AlarmPlayer + haptics.
fix: Android 14 revoked the default USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT grant for apps not classified as alarm/calendar. If the grant is absent the full-screen lockscreen alarm UI does not launch — the rider gets only a heads-up notification. Audio+vibration still fire, but the intended can't-miss lockscreen takeover degrades to a normal notification.

desc: GPS multipath in an urban canyon (elevated metro between highrises) produces a confident but WRONG fix that momentarily reads the rider inside the distance threshold, or snaps route progress backward/forward.
ev: No innovation/accuracy gating on the raw position that drives alarm timing: distance straight-line fires on distMeters<=threshold directly (alarm_controller.dart:447-460). The EKF's GpsDegradationDetector does innovation gating (gps_degradation_detector.dart:42-45, badInnovationSigma) but only inside sensor_fusion (line 159) and only affects EKF internal state, not whether the raw fix fires the alarm. SnapToRoute uses accuracy for soft-lock only on non-metro legs; metro legs 'effectively ignore position deviation' (trackingservice.dart:1120-1143).
fix: A spurious early alarm fires (minor), or a bad fix mis-advances/regresses snapped progress feeding a stop-count alarm, causing a mistimed alert.

desc: Cell-only / network-based coarse location (no satellite lock indoors or in a covered station) yields fixes with ~500-1500m accuracy while the stream keeps flowing.
ev: GpsHealthMonitor classifies accuracy>50m as degraded/unavailable (gps_health_monitor.dart:23-25,113) but is dead in production (only its own file + test reference it — confirmed via grep across lib/). Raw coarse fixes still flow through LocationManager (no accuracy floor, location_manager.dart) and fire alarms (alarm_controller.dart:425-460).
fix: Alarm evaluates against coarse fixes as if they were precise, firing at the wrong distance from the stop; degradation is detected internally but changes nothing.

desc: Rider prefetches a route above ground, then waits on the platform >5 minutes before the train arrives and descends where connectivity drops.
ev: RouteCache.defaultTtl = Duration(minutes:5) and get() returns null past TTL (route_cache.dart:62,130). OfflineCoordinator.getRoute throws StateError('Offline and no cached route available') when offline with no fresh cache (offline_coordinator.dart:165-178). The already-active route in the registry survives tracking, but underground reroute/refetch cannot recover.
fix: If any refetch/reroute is triggered underground, the cached route is past its 5-minute TTL so the cache returns null and the offline fetch throws, killing route-dependent recovery.

desc: Airplane mode is ON for the whole ride (common for battery saving on long commutes).
ev: Positioning relies purely on Geolocator/GNSS (gps_position_provider.dart, location_manager.dart) which functions in airplane mode; connectivity_plus flips offline (homescreen.dart:78-92) forcing cache-only routes (offline_coordinator.dart:165-178). No explicit airplane-mode branch; behavior is incidental, and cold-start latency (see A-GPS scenario) is unmitigated.
fix: GNSS still works receive-only so tracking can continue, but the app assumes no such distinction; with no network the initial A-GPS fix is slow and any route fetch requires a fresh cache, and there is no messaging that GPS is still viable.

desc: Rider uses a WiFi-only tablet or a cheap device with weak/absent GNSS hardware; WiFi drops once the metro leaves the station.
ev: No GNSS-hardware capability check exists; the app assumes Geolocator yields fixes (gps_position_provider.dart, location_manager.dart). Connectivity loss forces cache-only routes (offline_coordinator.dart:165-178) but nothing surfaces 'no positions arriving'. GpsHealthMonitor.unavailable exists but is unwired (gps_health_monitor.dart:11, dead in production).
fix: On devices lacking real GPS hardware there is no position source at all once WiFi network-location is gone, so no alarm ever fires; the app never detects the absence of a usable position source.

desc: Shallow cutting or elevated-to-underground transition where GPS flickers: one sparse fix every ~20-30s with gaps near gpsDropoutBuffer.
ev: Each arriving fix triggers exactly one eval (location_stream_handler.dart:268); between fixes there is no interpolation-driven firing. Distance-mode still fires on a late fix (alarm_controller.dart:447) but 'before the stop' timing is not guaranteed. gpsDropoutBuffer is 5s in-handler but overridden by policy to as high as 25s (trackingservice.dart:66, location_stream_handler.dart:199) before fusion even starts.
fix: The alarm can only fire on the sparse fixes; if the stop threshold is crossed between two fixes, the alert lands late (on the next fix, already past the stop) rather than before the stop.

desc: Repeat same-day identical journey or two simultaneously queued identical A->B routes (e.g. commuter queues the morning trip twice, or round-trip stored where the return has not yet reversed).
ev: route_session_manager.dart:134-139 RouteCache.makeKey called WITHOUT departureTime (makeKey supports it, route_cache.dart:87-104, but it's not passed). RouteQueue tracks only activeRouteIndex (route_queue.dart:9,28-31). AlarmController state is keyed by this colliding key (alarm_controller.dart:111-186).
fix: Route key omits departureTime, so identical origin/dest/mode collide on one key; the queued/second instance shares the first's fired alarm state, and destinationAlarmFiredForKey already true suppresses the destination alarm on the repeat -> missed stop.

desc: OS kills and restarts the service once mid-journey overnight WITH a valid snapshot (>30s in, directions present).
ev: trackingservice.dart:2020-2102 recovery path restores route via snapshot but never restores _firedLegIds/_destinationAlarmFired; trackingservice.dart:2009-2011 and location_stream_handler.dart:637-639 reset gating state; AlarmController fired-state is in-memory only (alarm_controller.dart:84-99).
fix: Recovery restores destination/mode/route but the fresh isolate's AlarmController has empty firedLegIds/destination flags and _timeAlarmEligible resets to false; already-passed transfer legs can re-fire spuriously, and a time alarm must re-earn the 100m/30s/3-sample gate, delaying it.

desc: Very short non-metro TIME journey that completes in ~30-120s and does cross 100m (short auto/bus ride).
ev: location_stream_handler.dart:602-605 eligibility thresholds; alarm_controller.dart:623-634 suppresses time eval until eligible. Gate protects against spurious early fires but has no upper bound relative to a tiny total journey.
fix: Alarm is gated until 100m + 30s + 3 samples elapse, by which point the rider may already be at/near the destination, so the 'N minutes before' warning arrives late or effectively at arrival.

desc: Long one-stop journey in TIME mode ('wake 30 min before') where a transient GPS speed spike (multipath at a station, brief 200km/h reading) momentarily collapses the ETA below threshold hours early.
ev: eta_engine.dart:14 speedAlpha=0.25 EMA and eta_engine.dart:291-309 smoothing dampen spikes (mitigation), but time-mode fires on a single smoothedETA<=threshold with no dwell/persistence requirement (alarm_controller.dart:680-711) and latches via setDestinationAlarmFiredForKey.
fix: A single momentary ETA dip fires the destination alarm early and latches it, so the rider is woken hours before arrival and the real arrival is suppressed.

desc: Elevated/underground mixed line or tunnel with open-air gaps where GPS flickers on and off repeatedly (typical of Delhi/Bangalore metro viaduct-to-tunnel transitions).
ev: gps_health_monitor.dart:14-20 (observation only), :102-133 (hysteresis thresholds); location_manager.dart:196-251 jitter/spike guards help but can't manufacture a fix; alarm still gated on GPS ticks (location_stream_handler.dart:267-273).
fix: Each brief reacquisition yields a low-accuracy, possibly jumped fix; GpsHealthMonitor needs 5s sustained degradation and 25s silence to change state (gps_health_monitor.dart:23-28,102-133), so rapid flicker keeps it oscillating near 'healthy' and the fusion/EKF is never authoritatively trusted. Because alarms only evaluate on GPS ticks, the alarm could fire on a single noisy re-fix at the wrong location, or not at all between flickers. The health monitor is also documented as pure-observation and 'does NOT trigger any behavioral changes.'

desc: Onboard metro WiFi (or a captive-portal WiFi) is connected; the phone's fused location provider leans on WiFi/cell positioning while underground.
ev: location_manager.dart:169-280 (no discrimination of GPS vs network/WiFi fixes); reroute depends on ApiClient/Directions (api_client.dart) but route is cached (route_cache.dart), so navigation continues offline.
