fix: Two risks. (1) Mid-journey network calls (Directions API reroute) can hang on a captive portal with no internet, but the route is prefetched so core tracking survives — this part is fine. (2) WiFi-based positioning can return a stale/biased 'open-air' fix inside a tunnel, feeding a wrong Position into the alarm check with high apparent accuracy; there is no source-tagging or WiFi-fix rejection (LocationManager treats all Positions identically, location_manager.dart:169-280). Could trigger an early or misplaced alarm.

desc: Loud media or another alarm app is already playing (rider dozed off with music/podcast, or a separate clock alarm) when the wake-up alarm fires.
ev: alarm_player.dart:13-24 (gainTransient, USAGE_ALARM), :84-87 (setVolume(1.0) is player volume, not system alarm stream); no AudioManager stream-volume boost.
fix: The alarm requests only transient focus (gainTransient) and routes to the alarm stream, which usually ducks media, but with gainTransient the other app may not fully stop and, if the device's ALARM stream volume is low while media is loud, the wake-up can be masked. The code forces alarm audio attributes and sets volume 1.0 (alarm_player.dart:66-95) but cannot raise the system alarm-stream volume, so a rider who lowered alarm volume gets a quiet alert.

desc: Doze / App Standby engages during a long stationary dwell (train held at a platform for many minutes, or the rider is waiting before departure with the phone idle and still).
ev: power_policy.dart:27-57 (low-battery tier coarsens GPS); location_stream_handler.dart:418-425 (timer-based checks assume the process is scheduled); AndroidManifest.xml declares no WAKE_LOCK (relies on plugin merge).
fix: Largely mitigated while the location-typed foreground service is alive (Doze exempts foreground services and the GPS-check timer keeps ticking, location_stream_handler.dart:418-425). Residual risk: on low battery the policy drops to LocationAccuracy.low + 50m distance filter + 40s dropout buffer (power_policy.dart:49-57), coarsening fixes right when precision matters, and on OEMs that ignore FGS Doze-exemption the timer can be throttled. No wake-lock is declared in the app manifest.

desc: NEW DIMENSION privacy / data-protection (India DPDP Act 2023 + store policy). The app continuously tracks fine location, persists route + position history to on-device Hive snapshots, sends origin/destination to Google Directions/Places, and declares an analytics/tracking intent (NSUserTrackingUsageDescription) — with no consent flow, no privacy policy surfacing, no data-retention/deletion control, and no account/data-export path.
ev: NSUserTrackingUsageDescription in Info.plist states analytics use, but there is no consent gate in lib. Location/route persisted via Hive snapshots (tracking_state_store.dart, route_cache.dart) and EKF/app logs (ekf_logger.dart, app_logger.dart) with only a developer 'export' — no user-facing clear-history / delete-my-data / retention limit. Privacy is absent from all 6 existing dimensions.
fix: Regulatory non-compliance (DPDP consent + right-to-erasure, Play/App Store data-safety disclosures) and user-trust risk. Persisted location history and diagnostic/EKF logs accumulate with no user-facing deletion; a shared/lost phone leaks the rider's travel patterns.

desc: NEW DIMENSION adversarial / abuse / misuse. Beyond the already-noted mock-GPS spoofing, the always-on covert background location tracker is a ready-made stalkerware primitive (install on a partner's/child's phone, it silently tracks and can be observed), and there is no protection against malicious/oversized route injection, notification abuse, or reverse-engineering of the Directions/Places API key.
ev: No position.isMocked check in the alarm path (consistent with the existing network-positioning LOW). Persistent tracking runs with a quiet/paused-style notification (notification_service.dart), i.e. low-visibility background tracking. No API-key restriction/attestation evidence. Abuse/stalkerware and adversarial-input classes are unconsidered.
fix: App is repurposed for covert surveillance (a real safety/abuse vector for an always-tracking, quiet-notification app), or a crafted/huge route or spoofed fix corrupts progress and mis-fires the alarm. No tamper/mock detection in the alarm path, no misuse safeguards.

desc: All permissions are demanded at the moment of arming the trip (Wake Me press) rather than during a calm onboarding — so the rider is already inside the moving metro/bus, on flaky connectivity, when told to leave the app and go to system Settings to grant 'Allow all the time'.
ev: Permissions are requested lazily inside _onWakeMePressed (homescreen.dart:481-483), not at install/onboarding. No pre-trip readiness screen exists. The background-location grant inherently requires a Settings excursion on Android 11+ (see permission_service.dart _requestBackgroundLocation), which is triggered at trip-start.
fix: The rider must background the app to fix Settings exactly as the journey begins; many abandon and start the trip with while-in-use location, which dies at screen lock. Worst-possible timing for a multi-step Settings trip.

desc: Infrequent rider uses WakePoint only for occasional travel. Android's 'auto-reset permissions for unused apps' (default) revokes location after a few months of non-use; the rider re-arms for a big journey.
ev: PermissionService.requestEssentialPermissions is invoked each Wake Me press (homescreen.dart:481), so foreground location and notification re-prompt with their _showSettingsDialog fallbacks. But _requestBackgroundLocation (permission_service.dart) still lacks any isPermanentlyDenied/_showSettingsDialog branch, so an auto-reset that lands background location in permanent-deny cannot be remediated in-app.
fix: PermissionService re-checks on each Wake Me press (good), but a revoked-to-permanently-denied background location dead-ends because _requestBackgroundLocation has no Settings path, silently blocking the trip; foreground-only revocation is recoverable but background is not guided.

desc: Rider denies (or the un-guided request silently fails for) ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION / HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS, which the EKF dead-reckoning relies on to keep tracking through underground metro tunnels.
ev: permission_service.dart _requestActivityRecognitionPermission() calls request() and ignores the result entirely (comment: 'less critical, so we can just request it'), returning void; requestEssentialPermissions treats it as non-critical. Manifest declares ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION and HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS but nothing educates or verifies. (Impact is latent since the task notes EKF is not yet wired into production alarm logic, but the permission gap is baked in.)
fix: When the train enters a tunnel and GPS drops, the EKF has degraded/no IMU input, so dead-reckoning over the known route underperforms — precisely the tunnel scenario the product exists to solve. The denial is swallowed with no user feedback.

desc: iOS rider, realizing they've been asleep, re-opens the app near/at their stop hoping the recovery/snapshot logic catches them up.
ev: snapshot_route_restorer.dart and _onStart null-initialData snapshot path (trackingservice.dart:2023) exist and can restore route state, but they only execute on app relaunch/foreground (onForeground: _onStart, trackingservice.dart:221). Nothing re-evaluates the alarm during the suspended window; restoration is reactive to the user opening the app.
fix: Snapshot restore only runs when the user manually foregrounds the app; by then the app may resume past the target stop with a stale last-known position, and there was no alarm during the gap. Recovery is user-initiated, not automatic — useless to a sleeping rider.

desc: iOS-specific notification permission handling: the app relies on the plugin's default Darwin prompt and its explicit permission flow skips iOS entirely.
ev: permission_service.dart:74-75 _requestNotificationPermission() returns true immediately for non-Android ('Not needed on iOS in the same way'), so there is no explicit iOS notification-permission verification; it relies solely on DarwinInitializationSettings() (notification_service.dart:563) default prompt with no follow-up status check or settings-redirect on denial.
fix: If the user dismisses/denies the iOS notification prompt (or it's never surfaced at the right time), even the one delivery mechanism that could work in-foreground is gone, and the app has no iOS-specific check or re-request to recover — compounding the background-execution gap with a delivery gap.

desc: Notifications for the app are muted or the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission is later revoked/never granted, so even a perfectly-alive isolate's show() call is silently dropped by the OS.
ev: Every alarm surface routes through _notificationsPlugin.show (notification_service.dart:818/906/968/1100/1202). USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is declared in the manifest but only used on the live in-isolate path; nothing pre-schedules a full-screen alarm via zonedSchedule/AlarmClock as an independent redundant channel, so a single muted/denied notification permission is an unrecoverable single point of failure.
fix: The live alarm notification is suppressed by the system and the rider is never woken; there is no alternative loud channel (e.g., a pre-scheduled full-screen-intent alarm) armed as redundancy.

desc: An elderly / cognitively-impaired first-time rider arms the alarm and wants to confirm it actually works before trusting it enough to fall asleep on a long ride.
ev: grep for test/preview alarm across lib/ returns nothing. lib/screens/ringtones_screen.dart _togglePreview() only calls _audioPlayer.play() — audio-only preview, no vibration preview, no full end-to-end wake-cue test.
fix: There is no 'test/preview alarm' that plays the real wake cue (sound + vibration + full-screen). The ringtone screen previews audio only, so a Deaf/HoH user gets no vibration preview and no one can validate the end-to-end cue. The rider either won't sleep (product fails to deliver its core value) or sleeps on a silently-misconfigured or imperceptible alarm.

desc: A TalkBack user toggles between 'stops/distance' and 'time' alarm modes using the mode switch on the home screen while arming.
ev: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1177-1188: Row([Text('Time'), Switch(value:_useDistanceMode...), Text(_metroMode?'Stops':'Distance')]) with no Semantics label or grouping; the switch value drives alarmValue/alarmMode computed at lines 630-641.
fix: The Switch has no semantic label saying what it controls; the reader announces only 'switch, on/off' between two loose Text labels ('Time' … 'Stops'/'Distance'), so the user cannot tell which position means which mode and can silently arm the wrong mode — e.g. '2' interpreted as 2 minutes instead of 2 stops — changing when the alarm fires.

desc: An elderly or low-vision rider tries to delete a wrong entry from their recent-destinations autocomplete list, or a motor-impaired rider tries to tap it.
ev: lib/screens/homescreen.dart lines 1126-1145: trailing GestureDetector(onTap:_removeRecentLocation) -> Container(padding: EdgeInsets.all(4)) with Icon(size:16), no Semantics/tooltip, no InkWell/IconButton min-target sizing.
fix: The delete affordance is a ~24px circular GestureDetector (icon 16 + padding 4) — below the 48dp minimum touch target — with no semantic label, so it is invisible to TalkBack and easy to mis-tap for anyone with reduced vision or dexterity; they cannot manage their saved locations and may repeatedly re-select a wrong destination.

desc: A low-vision rider (not fully blind, no screen reader) reads the arming screen and the fired-alarm screen in bright daylight on a cheap phone with a dim/low-quality display.
ev: lib/screens/homescreen.dart hintStyle Colors.white70/black54 (1099-1101), stepper container grey[200]/grey[700] (1228); maptracking.dart disabledBackgroundColor Colors.grey.shade300 / disabledForegroundColor grey.shade600 (1154-1157). No high-contrast mode and no MediaQuery.highContrast handling anywhere in lib/.
fix: Core text relies on low-contrast greys (white70/black54 hints, grey[200]-on-grey containers, grey.shade600-on-grey.shade300 disabled states) that fall below WCAG AA contrast, so the destination field hint, threshold text, and disabled 'Stop Alarm' state are hard to perceive; the rider may misread or fail to notice the control state.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Rider grants notifications at start, then the phone enters night-time Do Not Disturb / silent, or the rider revokes notification permission after tracking has begun.
ev: Permissions checked once at start only (lib/screens/homescreen.dart:482-483, gate at 491); no re-check during tracking. Mitigations: lib/services/alarm_player.dart:13-24 sets AndroidUsageType.alarm, and lib/services/notification_service.dart:726-731 sets Importance.max, category alarm, fullScreenIntent:true — but grep for setBypassDnd|bypassDnd returns no explicit channel DND-bypass, and no runtime DND/permission monitor exists.
fix: Permission and DND state are validated only once at journey start; there is no runtime re-check or 'you are no longer protected' warning. If the wake-up channel is suppressed by a scheduled DND profile the rider may not be woken. Mitigations exist (alarm audio usage + category=alarm + fullScreenIntent) but there is no explicit channel DND-bypass flag and no runtime verification, so the outcome is device/OEM-dependent rather than guaranteed.

area: Legal / liability / rider-safety of a failed or mi
desc: Deviation-triggered termination fires while the rider is asleep — e.g. carried well past the route and stopped 5km+ away. The app wakes them with the termination notification.
ev: lib/services/trackingservice.dart:1476-1494 shows title 'Tracking Ended' with body = raw termination userMessage; those messages (lib/services/tracking_termination_policy.dart:157-159, 172-174, 208-210) are diagnostic ('You appear to have stopped Xkm from your route' / 'heading away from your destination') with no actionable safety guidance, and allowContinueTracking:false ends tracking outright.
fix: The rider is woken in an unfamiliar and possibly unsafe location by a bare status message ('Tracking ended: You appear to have stopped X km from your route') that offers no orientation, no 'you may have missed your stop — check your surroundings / next return service' guidance, and no safety framing for a disoriented late-night rider. The wake is technically delivered but human-unsafe, and it doubles as the moment the product silently gives up.

desc: HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS is declared but there is no OEM-restriction / autostart handling for the screen-off scenario beyond the manifest permission.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml L12 declares HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS (a normal/install-time permission, correctly not runtime-requested). No MIUI/autostart handling found (grep for miui/xiaomi/autostart empty).
fix: Low priority; fold OEM autostart guidance into the battery-exemption onboarding step above.

area: Fire Decision + EKF consumption in the alarm path
desc: Hot-path debug I/O: the metro evaluator writes a file to app documents dir and emits large print() blocks on every GPS tick, a battery/latency cost over a 2h journey on a budget Android device.
ev: File append every evaluation (alarm_evaluator.dart:828-836 getApplicationDocumentsDirectory().then(... writeAsStringSync(..., append))); numerous print() at :152-153,:200,:244-250,:354-377,:825; plus estimateEtaSecondsToMeters print() at :1293-1453.
fix: Gate all print()/file writes behind a debug flag (kDebugMode) and remove the per-tick mumbai_alarm_debug.txt append.

desc: deviation_detection.dart is dead code whose offline-widening safety logic is NOT in the live deviation path, giving a false impression that off-route thresholds relax offline.
ev: grep shows isDeviationExceeded / findClosestPointOnRoute / determineThreshold are referenced only inside deviation_detection.dart itself — no production caller. The live path is DeviationMonitor with SpeedThresholdModel (deviation_monitor.dart:21-34, T_high=base+k*speed) which has no offline branch. So determineThreshold's 'baseThreshold = isOffline ? 1500 : 600' (deviation_detection.dart:50-57) never executes; offline off-route sensitivity is actually unchanged from online.
fix: Either delete deviation_detection.dart or wire its offline-aware threshold into DeviationMonitor so that off-route tolerance genuinely widens when GPS/connectivity is degraded.

area: Alarm Delivery (last-mile: making an audible sound
desc: Native leftover alarm channel mismatch (minor correctness/robustness). MainActivity.kt creates channel `geowake_alarm_channel_v3` at IMPORTANCE_HIGH, but the Dart code posts on `geowake_alarm_channel_v4` at Importance.max. The v3 channel is dead code; if any code path ever fell back to v3 it would be lower importance (no FSI/heads-up guarantee).
ev: MainActivity.kt createNotificationChannel() creates `geowake_alarm_channel_v3` (IMPORTANCE_HIGH); notification_service.dart:610 and :722 use `geowake_alarm_channel_v4` (Importance.max).
fix: Remove the unused v3 native channel or align it to v4/max to avoid confusion and any accidental low-importance fallback.

desc: Battery drains across tiers during a long journey (e.g. starts at 60%, drops to 15% during a 45-min ride).
ev: Battery is read once in location_stream_handler.dart:179-197 and trackingservice.dart:2122-2139 at stream start; _fftEnabled is latched at location_stream_handler.dart:200 (batteryLevel>=20). No listener updates the policy when battery_plus onBatteryStateChanged fires (that listener exists only for UI in homescreen.dart:197).
fix: Power policy (dropout buffer, notification tick, reroute cooldown) is fixed at journey start and never re-read, so timing parameters no longer match the actual battery state; FFT motion classification chosen at start is also frozen.

desc: Very old Android (API < 26/29) budget device where foregroundServiceType='location' and the newer permissions have no effect and Doze/background limits differ.
ev: AndroidManifest.xml service uses android:foregroundServiceType='location|mediaPlayback' (meaningful only API29+); HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS is API31+. minSdk is flutter.minSdkVersion (android/app/build.gradle:20), not pinned high. permission_service.dart requests location/locationAlways/notification/activityRecognition but there is no per-API-level branching or graceful degradation for the sensor-rate assumption.
fix: Foreground-service-with-location semantics and HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS/POST_NOTIFICATIONS are no-ops on old APIs; background execution guarantees weaken, raising the chance the service is throttled or the high-rate IMU the EKF expects is unavailable.

desc: Wi-Fi-only tablet or foldable used as the tracking device (no cellular/GNSS chip, or GPS only via network).
ev: location_manager.dart:94 unconditionally subscribes to Geolocator.getPositionStream; there is no check for GNSS availability or a coarse/network-only fallback strategy. Time-alarm eligibility requires real movement/speed samples (location_stream_handler.dart:601-607: moved>=100m, >=3 speed samples, >=30s), which a stationary/no-fix device never satisfies.
fix: GPS positions never arrive or are extremely coarse; time-mode alarm never becomes eligible and distance/stop progress never advances, so no alarm fires.

desc: Unscheduled SIGNAL HOLD / dwell far longer than modeled (train stuck in a tunnel between stations).
ev: alarm_evaluator.dart:1298-1404 estimateEtaSecondsToMeters prefers step-duration ETA when speed<=0.5 (ignores the hold); station_association.dart:104-118 re-anchors on any ZUPT dwell>=3s with a candidate in window.
fix: Stops-mode: progress does not advance while stopped, so no spurious fire and counting resumes correctly on movement — handled. Time-mode: ETA falls back to fixed modeled step durations when speed~0, so a long hold makes the app fire the N-minute alarm too EARLY relative to actual (delayed) arrival — an annoyance, not a miss. Secondary risk: if the hold happens near a modeled station, EKF ZUPT can false-anchor progress to that station and jump 's'.

desc: Rider gets off one stop early or changes their mind mid-route and leaves the train before the alarm has fired.
ev: On non-metro legs leaving the corridor triggers deviation/soft-lock and a reroute attempt (trackingservice.dart:1143-1172, _handleRerouteDecision:1310+), but metro legs deliberately ignore positional deviation (trackingservice.dart:1122-1143) so a mind-change on metro is not re-planned; alarm just stays bound to the original leg target. No spurious miss for the awake rider, but no adaptation either.
fix: Route progress freezes when they stop moving toward the destination, so the wake-up simply never fires — acceptable since they are awake. The real hole is if they then board a different train/line: the original alarm target is now meaningless and the app has no notion the plan changed on a metro leg.

desc: A mock-location / fake-GPS app (common in India for other apps) or GPS spoofing feeds fabricated coordinates.
ev: No position.isMocked check anywhere in the alarm path; positions flow unfiltered through LocationManager._processPosition (location_manager.dart:177-280) and drive alarms in alarm_controller.dart. isEstimated is hardcoded false for GPS (gps_position_provider.dart:43) with no mock/authenticity distinction.
fix: The app trusts spoofed fixes as real, firing the alarm at the wrong place or advancing progress incorrectly.

desc: Very short journey in DISTANCE mode where the chosen 'N km before' threshold is >= the whole remaining route at start (e.g. 800m trip with '1 km before').
ev: alarm_controller.dart:492-532 fires as soon as remainingMeters<=alarmValue*1000 with no minimum-progress gate (distance/stops modes have no eligibility gate — only time mode does, alarm_controller.dart:623).
fix: remainingMeters<=thresholdMeters is true immediately, so the destination alarm fires at the moment tracking starts (spurious-early); minor annoyance, and it consumes the single destination fire.

desc: DST change or timezone crossing mid-journey (spring-forward, or a border intercity into Nepal/Bangladesh time).
ev: India (India-first market) observes no DST and a single timezone, so this is largely N/A domestically. Where it applies, tracking_termination_policy.dart:136-173 uses now.difference(deviationStartTime).inMinutes and alarm_controller.dart:207-223 uses wall-clock DateTime differences; a forward jump could trip the sustained-deviation termination early. Core firing is progress-based so not directly affected.
fix: A wall-clock jump in DateTime.now() could make elapsed-duration timers (deviation-termination, cooldowns) compute negative/inflated durations, prematurely ending tracking or skipping cooldown.

desc: Temperature extremes (phone left in a hot bag / cold outdoor platform) degrade IMU/GPS sensor behavior, or a cheap phone thermally throttles the CPU, slowing the isolate.
ev: No thermal/PowerManager.ThermalStatus handling in lib; EKF calibration noted as single-ride (ekf_types.dart / sensor_fusion.dart tuning constants); timer cadence assumes timely scheduling (location_stream_handler.dart:418-425).
fix: No thermal or sensor-bias compensation exists, and the EKF is calibrated to a single Bangalore ride. Since the EKF is not wired into alarm logic anyway, the immediate blast radius is limited to degraded ETA/fusion quality; but thermal CPU throttling can delay timer ticks and GPS processing, widening effective dropout windows. Not explicitly handled.

desc: NEW DIMENSION multi-user / shared-device / remote-arming. India-common shared family phones and the realistic need to wake someone else (e.g. arm an alarm for a child or elderly parent riding, or hand the phone over) are unmodeled: there is no profile concept, and only one active journey/alarm state keyed by route with no per-user separation.
ev: Alarm/route state is single-tenant and keyed without a user dimension (route_session_manager.dart:134-139 makeKey without user; route_queue.dart tracks only activeRouteIndex). No profiles/accounts. This extends the existing 'repeat/identical-route key collision' timing-duration GAP into the multi-user case.
fix: On a shared phone, one family member's armed journey collides with another's (and the existing timing-duration key-collision GAP shows same-route state already clobbers), or a rider who wanted to arm on behalf of another person has no mechanism. Multi-user reality silently corrupts single-user assumptions.

desc: NEW DIMENSION monetization / commercial lifecycle. If/when the app monetizes (trial, subscription, ads), no thought is given to a subscription lapse or expired trial that fires MID-JOURNEY and could gate the alarm, an interstitial ad or paywall obscuring the wake screen, or offline riders being unable to validate entitlement underground. Currently there is no billing code at all, so the entire commercial-edge dimension is simply absent from the design.
ev: No billing/purchase/subscription SDK in lib (grep for in_app_purchase/BillingClient/StoreKit/entitlement empty). Because it is unbuilt, there is no fail-open guarantee that alarm firing is independent of any future entitlement/ads layer — a design hole to lock down before monetizing.
fix: A future entitlement check that fails closed (e.g. subscription expired at 3am, or offline receipt-validation underground) would block the alarm — turning a billing state into a missed stop. A paywall/ad over the full-screen alarm would suppress the wake cue. None of this is guarded against because monetization was never scoped.
